subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Blockage
object: The disposition of an object (the barrier) to prevent others from accessing, leaving, or seeing a restricted space, or group.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Deformation
object:
A process by which a physical Entity changes its shape under the influence of some factors outside of the Entity.

Note, changes of shape may be self-caused; for example, a gas will naturally disperse. This however would be a different type of process (Dispersion).

A soft slab of clay deforming under its own weight on Earth would still count as deformation: it is the gravity of the Earth (so, a factor outside the slab of clay) which makes the slab change shape.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#includesConcept
object: A relation recording that a Situation has a Concept as participant in some sort of role.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#involvesPlace
object: A relation recording that an Event makes some use of a PhysicalPlace. Typically this place is where the Event is located.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#LinkageState
object: Classifies States in which two objects are in a rigid connection, such that the movement of one determines the movement of the other.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SupportState
object: Classifies States in which an object is not able to move under gravity because of its placement relative to some other object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Approaching
object: A process type to classify motions by which a body approaches some object or location.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isAffectedBy
object: Simple relationship between two actions to express that a variation in the course or outcome of the object (the affector) would have resulted in a variation in the subject (the affectee), e.g., a planning task that sets parameters such as goal position affects the subsequently executed pick-and-place task that uses that parameter.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Extrinsic
object: A physical quality that depends on relationships to other objects, such as the color of an object which depends on light conditions in the environment.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Container
object: A role classifying an object used to contain others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Imagining
object: A Mental task in which the Agent constructs a mental representation of a possible world. An Agent performing an Imagining activity does not aim to construct a representation that aspires to be faithful to some past, present, or future state of affairs of the actual world it is embodied in.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PouringOnto
object: The task in which an agent pours the substance on top of an object

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affordsTask
object: Relates a disposition to the task defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl/manifestsIn
object: A relationship indicating that a Situation is realized in an Event that actually happened.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isQualityDescribedBy
object: Relates a description to a quality it describes.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Human-readable_Programming_Language
object: A Programming language like Java, Python etc. but not binary machine code.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Language
object:
A Language is a structured System for communication.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isGivenMeaningBy
object: The relation between an Information Object and a System that gives meaning to said object, e.g., a word, sentence, text, etc. might be given meaning by a Language and without the knowledge of said System (Language), the text will not make sense to a reader.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SocialQuality
object: Any aspect of an entity that specifies social characteristics.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Natural_Language
object:
A Natural Language is any language that has evolved naturally in humans through use and repetition without conscious planning or premeditation.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isOccurringIn
object: A relation between an event and an event type, e.g. 'taking the cup from the table' is an occurence of the motion 'approaching'.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#finishedBy
object: `A finishes B` means that A ends exactly where B ends, and that B strictly starts before A.  As in "I finish my day by taking a shower".

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isCausedByEvent
object: A relation recording that a Transition is the result of some Event.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasDisposition
object: Associates an object to one of its dispositions.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Programming_Language
object: Any Programming Language, including both human-readable like Java and non-human-readable languages like binary machine code.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#KnowledgeRepresentationLanguage
object: A Knowledge Representation Language is a Language with fixed semantics and syntax to describe some knowledge. Examples are JSON and the different OWL Profiles.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MovableJoint
object: A joint where the two connected links can move relative to each other in some dimension.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isFirstStepOf
object: A relation stating that some task is the first one in a workflow.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#JointLimit
object: The physical limits of a joint.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Retrospecting
object: A Mental task in which an Agent endeavors to construct a representation of a past state of affairs of the world it is embodied in.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Dicing
object: A particular kind of cutting where the goal is to produce small pieces out of some object or material. Unlike slices, the pieces to be obtained do not have one or two dimensions being more prominent than others. "Dice", the pieces dicing results in, are approximately cubic.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isOutputParameterFor
object: A relation between a Task and one of its output parameters.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Memorizing
object:
An atomic mental task in which an Agent saves some (declarative) information for later retrieval.

Examples include a student learning vocabularies or a computer saving some information to a database.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SubCognitiveAgent
object: An agent that is not capable to act on its own, i.e., that is reactive. Its intentionality needs to be bestowed upon from some other agent, that it acts for.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PrehensileEffector
object: An effector used to grasp objects, such as a hand of a human, or the long prehensile tail of a monkey.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#IncompatibleSoftware
object: A description of a situation where two software systems are incompatible with each other.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Replanning
object: A mental task, in which an agent reconfigures some plan that has been put together before.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RevoluteJoint
object: A hinge joint that rotates along an axis and has a limited range specified by the upper and lower limits.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasInitialState
object: A relation which connects a Transition to the Situation it starts from.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#GraspingMotion
object: A process type classifying a motion by which some end effector acquires kinematic control over some other object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasPositionData
object: Associates a spatial region to a position.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SourceMaterialRole
object: A role classifying a substance or object that enters a process of transformation intended to create some other object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasInitialSituation
object: A relation between SituationTransitions and Situations, which identifies the Situation the transition starts from.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#HeadMovement
object: The Agent moves a part of their body carrying high-bandwidth sensors such as cameras. The movement of other body parts is not significant.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#derivedFrom
object: The (transitive) relation between an information object and another which it has been derived from.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasFirstStep
object: A relation from a Workflow to its first Task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isOrderedBy
object: The relation between an 'Order item' and the 'Order' that sorts them (via the relations 'precedes' and 'follows')

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Algorithm
object:
An Algorithm is a finite sequence of well-defined instructions, typically used to solve a class of specific problems or to perform a computation.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algorithm

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SelectingItem
object: A task in which an Agent selects some object to use for a subsequent task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasLink
object: Relates an object to its kinematic components.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudKnowledgeTopic
object: A topic used when an Agent states some item of knowledge. This knowledge can be general, or specific to the environment and task at hand.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Shaping
object: The disposition of an object (the tool) to change the shape of others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasBinding
object: Asserts that in a context described by Description, a Binding relation holds.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasEventTime
object: Superproperty of hasEventBegin and hasEventEnd, records that an Event happened, or was happening, at a particular time. Using the subproperties captures the richer semantics of that time relative to the event. Using only this superproperty may be appropriate when the Event is construed to take place at a single instant of time.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Discourse
object: A mental task, in which two or more agents discuss some topic via multiple Illocutionary acts, which are part of this task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Slicing
object: A particular kind of cutting where the goal is to produce slices from some solid object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutionState_Paused
object: The execution state of a paused activity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ContainmentTheory
object:
A schematic theory that describes a functional relation which ensures that the location of some entity, the locatum, is constrained to be within some region which is the interior of some other entity, the relatum.

This is also known as FunctionalControlInternal in GUM-4-space (Bateman et al. 2010).

Let xL, xR be objects filling the locatum, relatum roles of this schema. Then one can infer that xL isInsideOf xR.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudPlanTopic
object: A topic used when an Agent describes what they intend to do. Note, this is not about describing the process through which this plan was constructed; that is covered by the MetaCognitionPlanningTopic.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalQuality
object: Any aspect of an entity that is dependent on its physical manifestation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Head
object: A functional part of the body responsible for carrying high bandwidth sensors, i.e., camera.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasEventEnd
object: A relation recording when an Event ended. In this case, we think of the Event as something unfolding over some span of time.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SituationTransition
object: A transition between two situations, usually brought about by the Action of some Agent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MentalTask
object: A Task classifying some MentalAction, that is, an Action through which an Agent manipulates representations stored in its own cognition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CommunicationAction
object: An action in which an Agent uses some actuator for communication purposes.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointVelocity
object: The velocity of a joint given in m/s (prismatic joints) or rad/s (hinged joints).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Shape
object: The external form, contours, or outline of an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isPerformedBy
object: A relation from an Action to the Agent who performs it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointPosition
object: The position of a joint given in m (prismatic joints) or rad (hinged joints).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Hand
object: A prehensile effector including palm, fingers, and thumb.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Transient
object:
Objects may undergo changes during Processes; however, while the change Process is in operation, one cannot strictly say either the input of the Process still exists, nor that the result exists yet.

A prototypical example is making a pancake on a heater. When PancakeMix is put on the hot plate, it ceases to be PancakeMix-- already, the chemical structure of the substance gets altered-- however it is only after sufficient heating that this object becomes a Pancake.

Transients are the objects undergoing such change processes; they are no longer the initial objects fed into the process, nor are they the objects produced as results.

Instead, a Transient transitionsFrom some initial Object that was fed into a change Process. Typically, a Transient may transitionTo some resulting Object (though not always, some processes simply destroy objects).

It is also possible that a Transient transitionsBack to the initial object. An example is the catalyst in a chemical reaction; another example is a loaf of bread after a slice has been cut off.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhaseTransition
object: An EventType that classifies processes by which matter changes from some distinguishable phase to another. We will use this to refer to the classical phase transitions between Solid, Liquid, Gaseous, Plasma etc. phases.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MetaCognitionEvaluationTopic
object: A topic used while an Agent describes its own cognitive processes and acions to evaluate them according to some metric.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FormalLanguage
object:
A Formal Language consists of words whose letters are taken from an alphabet and are well-formed according to a specific set of rules.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formal_language

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Closing
object: A task in which an Agent manipulates a container so as to block access to its interior.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SymbolicReasoner
object:
A Symbolic Reasoner, is a piece of software able to infer logical consequences from a set of asserted facts or axioms.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_reasoner

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isShapeRegionOf
object: Relates a shape to a physical object that has it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SelectedObject
object: An object chosen as the result of some selection task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Deposit
object: A role classifying an object ontop which others are put to e.g. store them, or to place them in a meaningful way for future activities.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Delivering
object: A task in which an Agent brings an item that the Agent already carries to a specified target.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#GraphDatabase
object: A Graph Database is a Database that uses graph structures for semantic queries with nodes, edges, and properties to represent and store data.

subject: Nb10d6409673545a7b05db6d6070c87d2
object: If something is an initial situation of some transition, then it must manifest.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Perceiving
object: A task in which the Agent gathers and interprets sensor information about its surroundings.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Localization
object: The localization of an object. The region of this quality encodes values to localize the object in a dimensional space, e.g. Euclidean positions that localize the object in Euclidean space.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Navigating
object: A task in which an Agent moves through space so as to arrive at some location, follow some path, or increase its distance from some location or other entity. Often, navigation involves finding paths around obstacles and forbidden areas.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ReleasingMotion
object: A motion by which a prehensile effector relinquishes kinematic control over an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Learning
object:
The mental task of storing information for later use.

This is more general than memorizing, as the later only captures declarative knowledge.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Variability
object: The disposition of an object (the tool) to change some aspect of others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#HingeJoint
object: A joint that rotates along an axis.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#BoxShape
object: A symmetrical shape, either solid or hollow, contained by six rectangles.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#replaces
object: The relation between a State that replaces another, e.g., the state of a bowl of fruits containing some objects is replaced by a new containment state when one object is taken away (in this example, we simplified the relation between the State and its type).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Selecting
object: A Task where an Agent decides between two or more options.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointEffortLimit
object: The maximum effort applied in a joint given in N (prismatic joint) or N*m (hinged joints).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasFilePath
object: Associates an entity to some file containing data about it. For example, can be used to describe physical objects via a mesh file.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ResultRole
object: A role classifying the object that is the outcome of a creation or modification action or process.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Succedence
object:
A relation that holds in some descriptive context such as a Workflow, between two TaskInvocations belonging to that same Workflow. It means that one task invocation should follow the other.

Note: a successor relation implemented as an OWL object property is sometimes enough, but not in general; in particular, when there are conditions imposed on the succession.

As a result, a reification pattern was applied here.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasInputParameter
object: A relation from an EventType (typically, a Task) and a parameter describing some state of affairs before the event classified by the EventType takes place, and which contributes towards that event happening.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTaskDefinedInAffordance
object: A relation between a Task and an Affordance, such that the task is defined in terms of using the affordance.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasPhase
object: A relation used to describe the structure of an Action or Process in terms of phases, i.e. subprocesses and states that occur during its unfolding.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Cuttability
object: The disposition of an object (the barrier) which makes it able to be cut down (into pieces) usually by some other object with role as a Cutter. Such as a cucumber has cuttability disposition which can be cut by a knife.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTaskOfOutputRole
object: A relation between a Task and one of its output roles.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ArchiveText
object:
An Archive is a Structured Text that is composed of one or more Structured Texts along with metadata. Archives are used to collect multiple texts together into a single text for easier portability and storage as Archive Files, or simply to compress text to use less storage space as Computer Files. Archive often store directory structures, error detection and correction information, arbitrary comments, and sometimes use built-in encryption.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archive_file

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FunctionalDesign
object: The design of an object from functionality point of view. A functional design is useful to develop complex modular objects with components that have a specific purpose, and can function with minimum side effect on other components of that object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Rubbing
object: The motion of an object sliding along the surface of another, for example, to clean the surface.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Option
object: The Role of objects that are used, e.g., in Selecting Tasks.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasTerminalState
object: A relation from a Transition to the Situation it ends in.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesSetpoint
object: Defines the dedicated goal region of a description.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Patient
object: A role classifying an object that undergoes/is the primary object affected by the event.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudTopic
object: A topic relevant for a think-aloud communication.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InsertedObject
object: An object inserted into another object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointPositionMax
object: The maximum position of a joint given in m (prismatic joints) or rad (hinged joints).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesInput
http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Instructions
object: The role of a plan to follow during an execution task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isLocalizationOf
object: Relates a localization quality to the object the localization belongs to.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MovingTo
object: A task in which an Agent moves towards a location.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DexterityDiagnosis
object: A description of the dexterity of a system, possibly in comparison to another system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasFrictionValue
object: The coefficient of friction denotes the ratio of friction force between touching objects. The coefficient is dimensionless.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RoleRoleBinding
object: A binding that asserts that two roles have the same filler.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalExistence
object: A State in which an Entity is said to exist in the physical world.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#metBy
object: A relation between entities, expressing a 'sequence' schema where one of the entities exactly ends where the other entity starts.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#UnavailableSoftware
object: A description of a situation where some software dependency is not available.

subject: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/DUL.owl#InformationRealization
object:
In SOMA-compliant systems, the way to use InformationObjects to specify extra data about an individual entity is to employ the 'is about' and 'expresses' properties (or their inverses 'is reference of' and 'is expressed by') and to supply a persistent identifier for a realization of the InformationObject.

As a prototypical example, consider an individual called Action_XYZ, about which we have some data for which the meaning is described by Description_ABC. The data would be an individual InformationObject_DEF, and the following property assertions would hold:

InformationObject_DEF 'is about' Action_XYZ
InformationObject_DEF expresses Description_ABC


Usually, an individual InformationObject would be connected to (at least) an InformationRealization individual. For example, suppose there is such an InformationRealization individual, InformationRealization_123. Then, this individual will have data properties describing its format and persistent identifier

InformationRealization_123 hasPersistentIdentifier 'doi'
InformationRealization_123 hasDataFormat 'urdf'

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MassAttribute
object: The quantity of matter which a body contains, as measured by its acceleration under given force or by the force exerted on it by a gravitational field.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FailedAttempt
object: A description of a failed attempt to achieve some goal.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CheckingObjectPresence
object: A task by which an Agent uses its sensors to check for the presence of a specific object and to obtain some other information about it, e.g. pose.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PouredObject
object: An object being poured into or onto some other object. A role of some fluid or substance that is the patient of pouring task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Fetching
object: A task in which an Agent retrieves an object from a particular location, which puts the object under the Agent's control, who can now e.g. transport the object somewhere else; this task may include repositioning the Agent to better reach the object. Note that while in normal linguistic use fetch can mean transport, we use it here to refer only to (a part of) the first stage of transport.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SourcePathGoalTheory
object:
A very general image-schema of the Path family, this schema describes movement along a path from a source towards a goal.

Note: in cognitive linguistics literature, the roles of this schema are Source, Path, Goal. However, to avoid overloading some other terminology in SOMA, we renamed Source to Origin and Goal to Destination.

As yet, this schema is not associated to any object property.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ActionExecutionPlan
object: links role and parameter fillers to e.g. slots in a data structure

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isDispositionOf
object: Associates a disposition quality to the object holding it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasNetForce
object: A relation between a physical object and the total force acting on it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#QueryAnsweringTask
object:
An Answering task that is the reaction to some Query answering task.

In a lot of cases, such a task is also an Assertion task, e.g., in the following discourse:

"How will the weather be tomorrow?"
"It is going to rain in the morning."

However, sometimes this might be not the case, e.g., with counterquestions.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RoleFillerBinding
object: A binding that connects a role to a particular filler.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CoveringTheory
object: A schematic theory of how an agent can use an instrument to prevent access to the interior of a patient.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ArtificialAgent
object:
A physical object with artificial characteristics, which can perform actions to achieve desired goals, and typically has sensors and/or actuators.

There can be non-physical artificial agents such as software programs but they are not considered here in the scope of artificial agent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Ontology
object:
An ontology encompasses a representation, formal naming, and definition of the categories, properties, and relations between the concepts, data, and entities that substantiate one, many, or all domains of discourse. More simply, an ontology is a way of showing the properties of a subject area and how they are related, by defining a set of concepts and categories that represent the subject.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontology_(information_science)

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhaseTransition
object:
The phase transition concept has also been more or less metaphorically applied in other contexts. An example from physics is the "jamming transition", and sometimes "phase transitions" are spoken of when describing problem spaces such as 3SAT.

In all these cases, the metaphor points to the existence of several regions of qualitatively different behavior (unimpeded passage of solid grains vs deadlock in a corridor; problem instances where the answer NO is trivial to prove vs. problem instances where the answer YES is trivial to prove), separated fairly sharply when some quantity reaches a threshold.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RelationAdjacentRole
object: A role classifying an object participating in some relation, e.g. a participant in a spatial relation or a linguistic fragment in a rhetorical relation to another.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasReferenceFrame
object: Gives the name associated to the local coordinate frame of a SpaceRegion.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#terminates
object: The association between an Event that terminates another Event, e.g., the Action of picking an apple from a bowl of fruits terminates the State of containment between the apple and the bowl.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ResourceRole
object:
A role classifying objects that are useful or even necessary to sustain the unfolding of an event.

Resources are usually not agentive; a different set of roles classifies the agentive participants in actions. Likewise, typically resources do not play causative or goal roles for the event.

Resources are often consumed by their participation in an event, but this need not always be the case. An instrument and capital are examples of resources that are reusable.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Distancing
object: A task in which an Agent increases its distance from some location.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointEffort
object: The effort applied in a joint given in N (prismatic joint) or N*m (hinged joints).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasNameString
object: A relation recording some identifier associated to an Entity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isPlanFor
object: A special relation between a Plan and a Task, to indicate that the Plan describes a way to achieve the Task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasAlterationResult
object: Relates an action that alters an object to the region that the alteration reached during the action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Answer
object: A role that is played by an Information Realization answering some query.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#movesObject
object: A relation from an agent to an object that the agent causes to move.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Tempering
object: The disposition of an object (the tool) to change the temperature of others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasPhysicalComponent
object: A relation used to describe the structure of a PhysicalObject in terms of physical components, i.e. what other PhysicalObjects are components of it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudSceneKnowledgeTopic
object: A topic used when an Agent describes what they know about their environment, including knowledge of world states that they do not currently perceive.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#orders
object: The relation between an 'Order' and the sorted 'Order item' (sorted via the relations 'precedes' and 'follows' between the 'Order item's)

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Preference
object:
A 'Preference' is a 'Quality' of an 'Agent' that orders 'Situation's by some heuristic based on the happiness, satisfaction, gratification, morality, enjoyment, and utility (see alse https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preference) they provide to their bearing Agent.

The pattern is as follows: A 'Preference' 'is described by' a 'Predilection', which also 'describes' an 'Order' that 'orders' 'Order item's that contain only 'Situation's. The 'Situation's then are modeled according to what the preference entails.

That a 'Preference' orders 'Situation's might be unintuitive, but makes the model very general. A few examples:

Example 1

"Peter likes coffee and dislikes tea".
Here, between different hypothetical situations where he plays the role of a performer in a drinking task, Peter prefers the situations in which role of the drunken object is played by some coffee (vs. some tea). Note that the coffe and tea are hypothetical objects as well and could, for example, be represented via reified Concepts.

Example 2

"Would you like this pot of coffee, or this pot of tea, Peter?"
Here, as opposed to Example 1, the pot of coffee and the pot of tea are not hypothetical, but concrete.

Example 3

"Would you like this pot of coffee, or should I brew you some tea?"
Here, the pot of coffee is concrete and the tea is not.

Example 4

Situations are not restricted to Tasks; other event types are possible as well.
For example, Peter might prefer the Containment State of a tiger being inside a cage vs. the Containment State of the tiger being outside of the cage.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#GoalRole
object: A role classifying objects that constitute the goal of an action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasSpaceRegion
object: Relates an entity to a space region.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AreaSurveying
object: A task in which an Agent uses its perception apparatus to gain information about some location.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ProximalTheory
object:
An image schematic theory that describes a qualitative spatial relation indicating relative proximity, as expressed by the prepositions 'near', 'close to', 'next to', etc.

It may seem that proximity is a very simple notion, requiring no sophisticated theoretical underpinnings. However, proximity is an extremely object- and purpose-dependent relation. A store next door is in a closeness relation to a person, and so is the Sun in the sky, despite the physical distances being different by several orders of magnitude.

As such, a theory, i.e. a description of what a particular kind of closeness means and in which contexts it applies, is necessary.

Adopted from GUM-4-space (Bateman et al. 2010).

Let xL, xR be objects filling the locatum, relatum roles of this schema. Then one can infer that xL 'near to' xR.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isSetpointAffordedBy
object: Relates a disposition to the setpoint parameter defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudObstructionTopic
object: A topic used when an Agent describes some state of affairs that prevents them from performing an action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PrehensileMotion
object: A motion of a prehensile effector.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasProcessType
object: A relation between roles and process types, e.g. a catalysator is needed to trigger some chemical reaction.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#EnclosedObject
object: An object included within the spatial boundaries of another object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isDefinedInAffordance
object: A relation between a Concept and an Affordance.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Triplestore
object: A Triplestore or RDF store is a purpose-built database for the storage and retrieval of triples through semantic queries.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PushingAway
object: A task in which an Agent pushes an object in front of themselves.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Barrier
object: A role classifying an object used to prevent others from entering or leaving a restricted space or group.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Disposition
object: The tendency of an object (the bearer) to make certain events happen with others (the triggers).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Destruction
object:
A process by which a physical Entity is destroyed.

Note, most of the physical Entities we are concerned with are actually arrangements of many smaller physical Entities, so another way to look at this is that a 'Physical destruction' is a process by which an arrangement of physical Entities, which was previously itself considered a physical Entity, is changed to such an extent that it is no longer recognized as continuing to exist.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isRecordIncludedBy
object: A relationship indicating that an InformationObject is a recording of an Event.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasEventBegin
object: A relation recording when an Event started. In this case, we think of the Event as something unfolding over some span of time.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Progression
object: A situation that sattisies a description of how a process evolves over time.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Temperature
object: The heat present in an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Capability
object: The tendency of an object (the bearer) to be able to perform certain tasks together with others (the triggers) and in which the Bearer is the executor of the associated Task and will therefore usually be an Agent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Driving
object: A process type classifying a motion of a body that exists because this body is attached to and controls some other moving body, usually a vehicle.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalBlockage
object: Classifies States in which an object, in general called restrictor, blocks access to an item. A usually agentive accessor, whose access is blocked, may be specified.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#directlyDerivedFrom
object: The relation between an information object and another which it has been derived from.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasSuccedence
object: A relation between a Workflow and a Succedence that appears in it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MixingTheory
object: A schematic theory about how an agent can mix a fluid or particulate object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasShapeRegion
object: A relation between physical objects and their shape attribute.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl/hasRequiredInitialSituation
object: A relationship between a Situation x and another Situation y that precedes it, such that without y manifesting, it would be impossible for x to manifest.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DeductiveReasoning
object:
A task in which the Agent, using general logical principles that it considers logically valid, applied to premises that it considers logically true, arrives at conclusions that it considers logically certain.

Deduction is often explained as starting from the "general" (some property X is known about all members of a set S), applying it to the "specific" (some Entity Y is known to belong to set S), to arrive at a specialization of the general property (X applies to Y).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ForgettingIncorrectInformation
object: A mental task in which the executing agent aims to correct its present information by deleting an incorrect information.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isConceptAffordedBy
object: A relation between a disposition and a concept defined in the affordance that describes the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#describesQuality
object: Relates a description to a quality that it describes.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Pouring
object: A task in which an agent lets liquid substance to flow out of an object. The agent has a kinematic control over the object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SchematicTheory
object:
A theory used to describe, analyze, and reason with the meaning of a linguistic message.

Note that such theories are useful both when analyzing an actual linguistic production, and when creating a linguistic production to describe some observed experience.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isProcessTypeOf
object: A relation between roles and process types, e.g. a catalysator is needed to trigger some chemical reaction.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Premise
object: The role of an object that is used to infer some conclusion via some inference rules.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ShapeRegion
object:
Encodes the shape of an object.

Note that sometimes the shape as actually used for some purpose may be displaced. This is the case, e.g., for robot links which use a mesh file to describe their shape, but the reference pose of the link uses the mesh translated/rotated in the link's local coordinate frame.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasParentLink
object: Relates a joint to the link it connects which is closer to the root of the kinematic chain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Reasoning
object: A Mental task in which an Agent endeavours to obtain new knowledge from knowledge it already possesses.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isProcessDefinedIn
object: A relation between a process type and a description that defines it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Labeling
object: A task in which an agent annotates some objects with names, e.g., labeling the feeling of a tip-of-the-tongue event as such.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutionState_Active
object: The execution state of an ongoing activity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTerminatedBy
object: The association between an Event that is terminated by another Event, e.g., the Action of picking an apple from a bowl of fruits terminates the State of containment between the apple and the bowl.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SoftwareDiagnosis
object: A diagnosis of the software of a system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Channel
object: A Channel in a Communication Task is the path of travel by a Message, e.g., via WLAN, air (in the case of a Message classifying soundwaves) or a telephone cable.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FunctionalSpatialSchemaTheory
object:
The superclass for theories describing functional spatial relations.

Adopted from GUM-4-space (Bateman et al. 2010).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Infeasibility
object: A description of a situation with a goal that is impossible to achieve in some situational context.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#coversObject
object: A relationship from an object (the coverer) that blocks access to another or its interior (the coveree).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ChemicalProcess
object:
A process by which the chemical constituency of an Entity or set of Entities changes.

In some sense any process that results in entities being created or destroyed might trivially fit here, however this concept is intended specifically for Events where the occuring chemical reactions are of importance.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isInitialSituationOf
object: A relation between SituationTransitions and Situations, which identifies the Situation the transition starts from.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PluginSpecification
object: The Specification of a Plugin interface defines how a Host and a Plug-in function together and exchange information.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#QualityTransition
object: todo(DB): added for NEEMs (quale change), but not sure yet about it...

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Containment
object: Classifies States in which an object is placed inside another.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Holding
object: A task by which an Agent keeps an object over which it has kinematic control, typically via grasping, at some specified pose.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasShapeScale
object:
The scale of a shape, given as a vector of three real numbers to adjust x, y, z components of vertex vectors. In cases where a shape needs to be flipped compared to the shape described by a mesh, one of the scale components will be negative. 

It is often the case that shapes need to be altered from their description in a shape file, and a typical example of this is scaling a mesh. 

In robotics, it is not uncommon to encounter shapes that are flipped compared to the shape in a mesh file. This is because robots often have bilateral symmetry, thus it makes sense to reuse the same meshes for corresponding links of the left and right arms.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Accessor
object: A role classifying an object used to gain access to some other entity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Squeezing
object: A task in which an Agent applies pressure to an object they have in their grasp.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Orienting
object: A task in which an Agent adjusts the orientation of an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudOpinionTopic
object: A topic used when an Agent expresses an opinion about the action they perform or the environment they are in.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ClientRole
object:
The Client-server model is a distributed application structure that partitions tasks or workloads between the providers of a resource or service, called servers, and service requesters, called clients Often clients and servers communicate over a computer network on separate hardware, but both client and server may reside in the same system. A server host runs one or more server programs, which share their resources with clients. A client usually does not share any of its resources, but it requests content or service from a server. Clients, therefore, initiate communication sessions with servers, which await incoming requests. Examples of computer applications that use the client-server model are email, network printing, and the World Wide Web.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Client%E2%80%93server_model

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Agonist
object: A role that classifies entities with a tendency to either cause an alteration or to preserve some state.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasInputParameter
object: A relation between a Task and one of its input parameters.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Instrument
object: An object used to carry out the event.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isMovedByAgent
object: A relation from an object to an agent who causes it to move.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalAction
object: An action performed by an agent by using its body in some way to interact with the physical world, e.g., through manipulation of objects, or by changing the posture.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isInsideOf
object: A spatial relation holding between an object (the container), and objects it contains.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Leaning
object: An Agent pitches its body in some direction.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Tapping
object: A motion, usually repeated several times, for example, to probe the surface of an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isShapeOf
object: Relates a shape quality to the object the shape belongs to.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DesignedComponent
object: An object designed to be part or element of a larger whole.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTaskOfInputRole
object: A relation between a Task and one of its input roles.
