subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#nickname
object: Similar to rdfs:label, but without GUI or reasoner impact in Protege; avoiding Protege problems is why this is not a label subproperty. Nicknames are used by particular software working with the ontology as a way to give community-specific names to concepts. Communities are identified by the subproperty of nickname.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SettingGripper
object: A task by which an Agent arranges one/some/all of its grippers in some configuration.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FunctionalPart
object: Parts of an agent or an artifact are considered as functional parts.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesProcess
object: A relation between a description and a process type.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#LinkedObject
object: An object that is linked to some other object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#encapsulates
object: The relation between an Ordered element' and an 'Entity' it contains.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Creation
object:
A process by which an Entity is created in the physical world.

Note, most of the physical Entities we will be considering here are in fact arrangements of many other, smaller physical Entities. Therefore another way to look at this is, a 'Physical creation' is the process by which a set of physical Entities is arranged in a certain way, and the arrangement is then itself considered a physical Entity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#HeadTurning
object: A process type classifying a motion of an Agent's head such that the direction this head faces changes relative to the facing direction of the Agent's body as a whole.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#transitionsTo
object: A property which relates a Transient to an Object it changes into. This is useful to model objects which, through participation in a process, transform themselves so that an ontological reclassification is necessary. An example of this is baked dough eventually becoming bread by completing a baking process.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FixedJoint
object: A joint that cannot move, designed to fixiate links.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FluidFlow
object:
A process by which a fluid moves or is moved from a location to another, but such that it maintains its constitution. A fluid is an Entity made of many smaller Entities, loosely bound to each other.

An issue to highlight here is the maintenance of constitution. Fluids-- gases in particular-- are prone to disperse. Such a process is not flow however, because the loose bounds between the constituents become even looser, to the point of the original Entity becoming entirely discombobulated.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasPersistentIdentifier
object: A property linking an InformationRealization to a persistent identifier such as a DOI, which can then be used to obtain an address at which the realization (i.e. digital file) can be retrieved.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasExecutionState
object: A relation from an Action to its execution state.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#HostRole
object:
In the Plug-in-Host pattern, a Host application provides services which the Plug-in can use, including a way for Plug-ins to register themselves with the Host application and a protocol for the exchange of data withPplug-ins. Plug-ins depend on the services provided by the host application and do not usually work by themselves. Conversely, the host application operates independently of the plug-ins, making it possible for end-users to add and update plug-ins dynamically without needing to make changes to the host application.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plug-in_(computing)

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Reasoner
object:
A Reasoner is some Software that can infer new, implicit knowlegde from explicitly stated knowledge.

This definition is broad and we consider any System fitting the above description as reasoners. For example, the following can be seen as Reasoners:
* A simulation, where the explicit knowledge corresponds to the initial situation, and the implicit knowlegde corresponds to the situation that is derived from that by simulating some unfolding processes.
* A machine learning algorithm, e.g., an image classifier: The explicit knowledge is the visual content of a picture (even down to the pixel), the implicit knowledge is the derived classification.
* A logic based rule engine, where initial facts are the explicit knowledge, and derived facts are the implicit knowledge.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Item
object: A role played by a non-agentive object operated on by an action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affordsBearer
object: Relates a disposition to the bearer role defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Sharpness
object: The quality of having a thin edge or point that can cut something or make a hole into something. It is worth to note here that the social aspect of sharpness such as the quality of being clear, intelligent etc is not considered as sharpness according to this definition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Dreaming
object: Any form of re-processing episodic memories for long-term memory by natural or aritifical agents.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Actuating
object:
Tasks where the goal is to move an object.

Usually, an agent will use their prehensile effectors, ie. hands, for this purpose, so there is a lot of conceptual overlap between Actuating and Manipulating.

However, these categories are nonetheless distinguished in that there are more ways to actuate objects than simply manipulating them; for example, some tool like a net or frying pan might be used to catch an object.

Another way to look at the difference between Actuating and Manipulating is in what they "profile", ie. focus on as important.

For Actuating, it is the object's motion that is paramount.

For Manipulating, it is the movement of the hand(s) and the change in functional relationships (such as kinematic control) between the hand(s) and the manipulated object(s).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FunctionalDiagnosis
object: An internal diagnosis of a system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasTask
object: A relation to indicate that a Task is part of a Workflow or ordering Relation: that is, the task may be executed during the execution of the Workflow, or there exists some Relation between the Tasks that informs how their executions are to be located in time.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasIntervalEnd
object: A relation recording when a TimeInterval ended.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affordsTrigger
object: Relates a disposition to the trigger role defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AssumingPose
object: A task by which an Agent arranges its body, or part of it, according to some configuration.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasColorValue
object: Associates a ColorRegion to numerical data describing the color.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExistingObjectRole
object:
A role that requires of its filler simply to exist, unlike other roles that may demand e.g. agentive or instrumental participation in some executable schema or plan (AgentRole and Instrument respectively).

The intention behind such a simple role is to have a way to represent, in a schematic formalism used to describe some scene, that an object is present. In particular, the schema used to convey this information is the ESTSchemaTheory, which has ExistingObjectRole as its sole defined role.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasIntervalTime
object: Superproperty of relations used to connect moments in time to a TimeInterval.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#LimbMotion
object: An Agent moves its limbs in some way.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasOutputParameter
object: A relation from an EventType (typically a Task) to a Parameter describing an outcome of the event classified by the EventType.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasMassAttribute
object: A relation between physical objects and their mass.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MetacognitiveControlling
object: The concious or subconcious task to control the own mental processes, e.g., evaluating them and instructing the own mind to shift attention.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DeclarativeClause
object: A clause which makes an assertion or declaration.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isOntopOf
object: A spatial relation holding between an object (the deposit), and objects that are located ontop of it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Room
object: Space that can be occupied or where something can be done.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Text
object:
Any Information Object defined using a Language that, when realized through a symbolic writing system, can be read and made sense of.

One may define Text as anything that can be made sense of, including e.g., Speech or Paintings.

However, the argument can be made that Speech or Paintings are not considered Text as they cannot be EXACTLY realized by a symbolic writing system: Speech may loose punctuation, Paintings their original appearance.
On the other hand, this might not be true as both could be encoded in a binary format that can be interpreted using a language (eg., mp3, png).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isContainedIn
object: The inverse of the contains relation. See the contains relation for details.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Alteration
object: A process by which an aspect of some object changes such as ice cream melting in the sun.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isOutputRoleOf
object: A relation between an output roles and its Task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#QueryEngine
object: A Query Engine is a Software that can answer some queries.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Joint
object: An object that is used to articulate links in a kinematic structure.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasStatus
object: A relation from an Entity to a Quality that is indicative of the Entity's state, e.g. if it is a device, its state of operation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SpatialRelationRole
object: Roles classifying entities participating in some spatial relation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#IncludedObject
object: An object that is contained in something. This is meant very general and includes, e.g., elements contained in a set, or things that are spatially contained within the boundaries of some object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Interpreting
object: A task in which an Agent interpretes some information, e.g., makes sense of some incoming message or its visible surroundings.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#symbol
object: An annotation property which should be used to record by what symbols or abbreviations, if any, some relation or entity is known in scientific literature.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AestheticDesign
object:
A design that describes an aesthetic quality of an object.

Aesthetics is the philosophical study of beauty and taste. The term stems from the Greek word 'aisthetikos', meaning 'of sense perception', and is related to the study of sensory values. From design point of view, aesthetics refers to the visual attractiveness of an object. Visual aesthetics have these key elements: Color, Shape, Pattern, Line, Texture, Visual weight, Balance, Scale, Proximity and Movement.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PreferenceOrder
object: The relation between a 'Preference' and the 'Order' that the 'Preference' defines over Descriptions of Situations.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ClausalObject
object: A clause is a phrase containing a subject and a predicate.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicsProcess
object: A process involving physical objects and phenomena which does not change the chemical constituency of the affected objects.

subject: N971032fa4ad84f95994986526d836e0b
object: If a transition has an initial situation then it also has a manifestation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Pulling
object: A task in which an Agent moves an object in a direction loosely from the object's center of mass towards the contact point between agent and object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Prediction
object: A Mental task in which the Agent endeavours to construct a representation of a future state of the world. Prediction commits itself to some degree of accuracy: the Agent believes that eventually something similar to the predicted state will come to pass.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudActionTopic
object: A topic used when an Agent states what they are doing.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasLocalization
object: Relates an object to its localization quality.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Inability
object: A description of a situation with a goal that some system is unable to achieve.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExcludedObject
object: An object that is not contained in something. This is meant very general and includes, e.g., elements excluded from a set, or things that are spatially excluded from the boundaries of some object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Scene
object: Scenes are Situations which interpret a State in terms of its conformance to some qualitative, image schematic description. I.e., the scene is described in terms of qualitative functional and spatial relations existing between participating objects.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Locomotion
object:
Conceptually related to Navigation, but distinguishable from it because of the profile, ie. the focus of the task.

Navigation is about reaching some goal.

Locomotion is concerned more with the actual motion.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Limb
object: An arm or leg of an embodied agent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Receiver
object: The role played by an Agent in a Communication Task that perceives and interpretes some incoming Message.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ESTSchemaTheory
object:
A schematic theory that describes the existence of an entity.

Developmental psychology posits that "object permanence" (the assumption that physical objects keep existing even when the agent doesn't perceive them, which consequently informs reasoning about where an object should be, even when perception of it is lost) is a cognitive ability that is not, at least in the very young human child, immediately manifest. Rather, it seems learned via interaction, and usually is among an infant's cognitive repertoire by age 2.

In SOMA, we represent this ability of a cognitive agent as an ability to generate and maintain ESTSchemaTheories. Each instance of such a theory refers to one particular physical object, the one that the instance of the ESTSchemaTheory asserts to exist.

Because each instance of an ESTSchemaTheory refers to a single object, ESTSchemaTheories are not associated to any relation between OWL individuals.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl/prevents
object: A relationship indicating that a situation does or would prevent another from manifesting. Useful for reasoning about planning (what to do to avoid some bad outcome) and failure recovery (what aspects of the world state prevent continuing the plan?).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Deciding
object: A mental task in where an agent makes some decision, that is, selecting some Information object; usually on the basis of others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Grasping
object: A task in which an Agent uses its end effectors to grasp an object, thus gaining kinematic control over it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FailWFNoContinuation
object: A particular kind of failure: the workflow fails because there is no way to continue it, and the normal exit has not been reached.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Reification
object: A description that *describes* a formal entity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MetaCognitionTopic
object: A topic for a description that an Agent might make of its own cognitive processes and actions.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#HasQualityRegion
object: The relation between an individual quality and a region.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Purification
object: The disposition of an object (the tool) to change the cleanliness of others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PlacingTheory
object: A schematic theory of how an agent can place a patient at a particular goal location.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Effort
object: A parameter describing the amount of force to be exerted by some actuator.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Successfulness
object: A description of a situation with a goal that was achieved by some system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasShapeParameter
object: Associates a SpaceRegion to some parameter value describing its shape. This is a fairly generic property, and to capture the semantics of the information associated to the SpaceRegion, its more specific subproperties should be used.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Swimming
object: A motion of some body through water. The body provides the power for the motion.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#givesMeaningTo
object: The relation between a System and Information Object that is given meaning to by said system, e.g., a Language might give meaning to some word, sentence, text, etc., but without the knowledge of said System (Language), the text will not make sense to a reader.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Vaporizing
object: Transitions from a solid to a gaseous phase are usually referred to as Sublimation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#StimulusRole
object: A role classifying an object that is perceived by some agent and thus triggers some reaction (e.g., a perception event).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Singleton
object: A 'Set' that contains exactly one member.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Linkage
object: The disposition of an object (the linked object) to establish a connection with others by being linked together.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ContainmentState
object: Classifies States in which an object is kept inside another object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InformationRetrieval
object:
A mental task in which an Agent recalls some knowledge that has been memorized previously.

Examples include a human remembering some information or a computer retrieving knowledge from a database.

The difference to Remembering is that for this Task, we are concerned with knowledge about a previous world state. Memory Retrieval is more general in the sense that it also includes the retrieval of learned facts and rules.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#during
object: `A during B` means that B strictly starts before, and ends after A, i.e. A is wholly contained in B.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#supports
object: A relation between an object (the supporter) and another object (the supportee) where the supporter cancels the effect of gravity on the supportee.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#StructuralDesign
object: A design of an object which describes its stability, strength and rigidity, and considers the way in which parts of an object are arranged.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AlterativeInteraction
object: A force interaction where the agonist has the tendency to set another object into motion. An example is 'opening a door' where some object interacts with the door such that it moves out of its frame.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ForceAttribute
object: The value of a force dynamical characteristic. An example is the force exerted on another object when pushing it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Constructing
object: A task in which an Agent creates a new physical object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Simulating
object:
A Mental task in which the Agent endeavours to create representations of a sequence of states of affairs in the world. Simulation commits itself to some degree of transition accuracy: supposing the actual state of the world was the initial state of the simulation, the world state and simulation state should evolve to some degree similarly.

Simulation does not commit itself to state accuracy: the initial state of the simulation is not constrained to be faithful to the actual state of the world in which the Agent is embodied. Counterfactual simulation ("what would happen if--?") is possible.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasOutputParameter
object: A relation between a Task and one of its output parameters.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isCoveredByObject
object: A relation from an object (the coveree) which is itself, or has its interior, prevented from being accessed from outside by a coverer.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Ontology_Language
object:
An Ontology Language is a Knowledge Representation Language to describe knowledge about properties of a subject area and how they are related, by defining a set of concepts and categories that represent the subject using logic. Examples are the different OWL Profiles.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontology_(information_science)

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesTrigger
object: Relates an affordance which is a relation between a bearer and a trigger, to the role of the trigger when the affordance is manifested.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#TimeRole
object: A role filled by a description of the location in time and/or duration of an event or object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Gripper
object: A mechanical device that grasps and holds things.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#VideoData
object: An information object containing data for audio-visual modalities.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Assembling
object: A task in which an Agent connects some objects such that they form a cohesive whole, and which also imposes constraints on the objects' relative motions. Often, the objects that make up an assemblage can also be separated again.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#finishes
object: `A finishes B` means that A ends exactly where B ends, and that B strictly starts before A.  As in "I finish my day by taking a shower".

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Dirty
object: A cleanliness region with values considered as dirty.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#includesSituation
object: A relation recording that a Situation has a (sub) Situation as participant in some role.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isDepositOf
object: A spatial relation holding between an object (the deposit), and objects that are located ontop of it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CanCut
object: The disposition of an object (the tool) to cut other objects. Such as a knife has cutting ability to cut a cucumber into pieces.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Choice
object: The output of a, e.g, Selecting Task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTerminalSituationOf
object: A relation between SituationTransitions and Situations, which identifies the Situation the transition ends at.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RecordedEpisode
object: An episode which has been recorded.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Arranging
object: A task in which an Agent places a collection of objects at some set of relative poses to each other.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isReplacedBy
object: The relation between a State that is replaced by another, e.g., the state of a bowl of fruits containing some objects is replaced by a new containment state when one object is taken away (in this example, we simplified the relation between the State and its type).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointParameter
object: Assigns a value for an attribute of a joint.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affordanceDefinesTask
object: A relation between an Affordance and a Task

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Retrospecting
object:
Done by analogy with Prospecting. Currently mono-subcategory, but perhaps we might find more.

As an example, a kind of Abductive reasoning would fit here: reconstruction, in which the agent attempts to create a representation of a past state of affairs which the agent has not actually observed, based on traces and clues surviving to the present.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#BlockedObject
object: An object that is blocked from accessing something.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#overlappedBy
object: A schematic relation between any entities that also implies ordering, e.g. "she has worked into the night".

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SpatioTemporalRole
object: Roles that classify entities which locate an event or object in space and time.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Standing
object: A motion by which an Agent arranges its body in an upright configuration. Typically, it makes sense to speak of standing for bodies where some limbs are dedicated to moving the whole body while some limbs are used for manipulation of other objects.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isBearerAffordedBy
object: Relates a disposition to the bearer role defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutionState_Succeeded
object: The execution state of a succeeded activity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Turning
object: A motion by which an agent changes which way their body faces.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isJointLimitOf
object: Relates a joint to its physical limits.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Walking
object: An agent, under its own power, moves over some solid surface.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DependentPlace
object: A feature that is not part of its host, like a hole in a piece of cheese.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isSourceFor
object: The (transitive) relation between an information object and another which was derived from the former.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CleanlinessRegion
object: Encodes the cleanliness of an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasIntervalBegin
object: A relation recording when some TimeInterval started.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasStep
object: A relation between a Workflow and a Task it contains.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Sender
object: The Role played by an Agent in a Communication Task that emits some Information Realization with the purpose of percipience by some Receiver.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutableSchematicTheory
object:
Also known as "executing schemas" or "x-schemas", these were defined by Bergen and Chang in their work "Embodied Construction Grammar in Simulation-Based Language Understanding" as:

"Executing schemas, or x-schemas, are dynamic representations motivated in part by motor and perceptual systems (Bailey 1997; Narayanan 1997), on the assumption that the same underlying representations used for executing and perceiving an action are brought to bear in understanding language about that action. The x-schema formalism is an extension of Petri nets (Murata 1989) that can model sequential, concurrent, and
asynchronous events"

SOMA does not restrict the formalism of ExecutableSchematicTheories; i.e. they don't have to be Petri Nets.

They maintain their role however as representations able to drive a simulation, at some level of abstraction, of an embodied action. This level of abstraction may be still fairly underspecified as in the case of the original x-schemas and as such not a plan that an agent could run in an actual physical environment without further information.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasForceValue
object: A value that quantifies a force given in Newton.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Conclusion
object: An object that is derived from some premise using some inference rules.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#transitionsFrom
object: A property which relates a Transient to an Object it changes from. This is useful to model objects which, through participation in a process, transform themselves so that an ontological reclassification is necessary. An example of this is dough undergoing the Maillard reaction through baking.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#KinoDynamicData
object: An InformationObject containing data about how a physical object is put together such that its parts may move relative to each other, and what the physical characteristics of those parts are.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CoverageTheory
object:
A schematic theory of a functional relation between two objects such that one of them, the locatum, blocks access to the interior of the relatum.

Let xL, xR be objects filling the locatum, relatum roles of this schema. Then one can infer that xL coversObject xR.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasColor
object: Relates an object to its color quality.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Reaching
object: A task in which an Agent moves one or more of its arms towards a location or object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DeviceState
object: A quality belonging to a device which indicates its overall functional state.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Reasoning
object:
todo: a taxonomy of reasoning is not trivial. Classical theory distinguishes Deductive, Inductive, and with a stretch Abductive reasoning. However, modern practice distinguishes other categories that overlap with these, e.g. Probabilistic and Non-monotonic.

Both Abductive and Inductive inference may, and often do, use Probabilistic methods. Probabilistic inference is, by its nature, most opposed to Deductive inference which, classically, requires logical certainty.

Any of the Abductive/Deductive/Inductive triad can be further affected by the Monotone/Non-monotone distinction. There are preferences (Inductive and Abductive reasoning is probably most often non-monotonic; most of Deductive reasoning is probably done in monotonic formalisms), but it is certainly the case that, e.g., non-monotone Deduction is possible.

Note, this classification has nothing to do with reasoning domain (e.g. SpatialReasoning, TemporalReasoning, ...) and merely with techniques/logical-mathematical underpinnings.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InterrogativeClause
object:
A clause which makes a request, typically information, of some agent.

Note that in a semantic sense such clauses always request information, but in a pragmatic sense they can be used to convey commands or requests for action, such as e.g. "can you close the door?" The question is not just a request for information about ability, but a request to perform a task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Antagonist
object: A role that classifies entities that are opposed to the tendency of some agonist.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#startedBy
object: `A starts B` means that A starts exactly where B starts, and that A strictly ends before B. As in "I start my day with a coffee".

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasDataFormat
object: A property linking an InformationRealization to a string specifying a format name, e.g. URDF or STL.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PrecisionGrasp
object: An Agent grasps an object, and focuses on obtaining precise kinematic control over it. This is useful for then following precise movements, e.g. when writing.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#causes
object:
Simple relationship between two actions to express that the object (the reaction) would not have occured if it were not for the subject (the cause), e.g., a Communication Action classified as an Querying Task causes another Communication Task classified as an Answering Task and the latter would not have occured without the former. An example without Agents involved is some domino stone that would not have toppled without the first one toppling.

When Agents are involved, the relation might be seen as an abstraction of the execution of some plan that arises from changing the agents goal that is due to perceiving the cause. However, currently it is unclear how to model such a pattern and therefore not included in SOMA.

This relation is seen as transitive.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CommunicationTask
object:
A Task in which two or more Agents exchange information. A CommunicationTask classifies only Events that have only Agents and Social objects as participants.

Of course, the means of exchange is Physical, however this concept is to classify events for which we are not interested in the physical substrate, but rather who communicated and what the information content was.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isInputParameterFor
object: A relation from a Parameter to an EventType (typically, a Task). The parameter describes some state of affairs that precedes and will contribute to the event classified by the EventType.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#State
object:
States are stative and homeomeric events.

For stative events, the mereological sum of two instances has the same type as both instances. This is, for example, the state of sitting on a chair, or the process of a pendulum swinging around.

The difference between states and processes is that states are, in addition, homeomeric, and processes are not.  This means that, when considering time slices  of an event, for states, these time slices always have the same type as the state, but for processes this is not the case.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointLimit
object: Relates a joint to its physical limits.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InterfaceSpecification
object:
The Specification of an Interface between software, computer hardware, peripheral devices, humans and combinations of these.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interface_(computing)

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DirectedMotion
object: A Motion that is considered to be toward a location or along a path. It is not important that the final location or path be the intention of some Agent, but it is considered that the important feature of this Motion is that it has a path and/or destination.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isPlanFor
object: Note that DUL already says Plans can define Tasks, but that relation is used differently: a Plan defines a Task because it contains it as a step.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isSupportedBy
object: A relation between an object (the supporter) and another object (the supportee) where the supporter cancels the effect of gravity on the supportee.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#3DPosition
object: A point in three dimensional space, given as translation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasPredecessor
object: Indicates that a Task is the predecessor in a Succedence Relation; that is, this is the task to execute first.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Manipulating
object:
Tasks where the goal is to move the prehensile effectors, ie. hands, of an agent so as to achieve some spatial or functional relation with some manipulated object. 

Spatial relations refer to positioning the hands in certain ways relative to the manipulated object, for example nearing or distancing them, or aligning them with some relevant axis.

Functional relations here refer to interactions between the hands and manipulated object which constrain the possible behavior of the object. Examples of functional relations in manipulation are support and kinematic control.

Note that manipulation tasks are usually performed with the intention of moving an object in some way, so there is a large conceptual overlap between Manipulating and Actuating.

However these concepts are nonetheless distinguished in what they "profile", ie. what they focus on as particularly important.

Actuating profiles the movement of the object itself.

Manipulating profiles the movement of the hands and the functional relations, such as kinematic control, they establish with the manipulated object.

Note: we employ Manipulating here in its literal, original sense, of using hands for some purpose, and not in the metaphorical sense of exerting psychological pressure on someone.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isReificationOf
object: An auxiliary property that is used to generate object individuals, called reifications, from any other Entity, e.g. from relations, classes, data types. These reifications can then be used in DL axioms as any other named individual.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Impediment
object: The disposition of an object (the obstacle) to prohibit certain ways of entering or leaving a space or group. An example is a doorstopper constraining a door, prohibiting it to enter the area behind it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl/hasExpectedTerminalSituation
object: A relation between a Transition and the Situation it is expected to, and does actually, end at. You can assert this relationship when the observed outcome of a transition matches expectations.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isDirectSourceFor
object: The (transitive) relation between an information object and another which was derived from the former.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#HardwareDiagnosis
object: A diagnosis of the hardware of a system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Cutting
object: The goal of this task is to separate one or more pieces from some target object by means of cutting into its constituent material. Unlike a disassembly, a cut is usually not easily reversible.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RelationalQueryLanguage
object: A Query Language that is designed for communication with some Relational Database.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PouringInto
object: The task in which the agent pours the substance into another object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesBearer
object: Relates an affordance which is a relation between a bearer and a trigger, to the role of the bearer when the affordance is manifested.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#StoredObject
object: An object being stored into some other object, usually inside a container.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Digital_File
object: Any file that exists as a digital resource (but not its content), e.g., a text file actually laying on some hard drive, but not the contained text.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Boiling
object: In each instance of this collection some liquid matter is raised to its boilingPoint and is thereby changed from being in the Liquid-StateOfMatter to being in the Gaseous-StateOfMatter.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isSetpointDefinedIn
object: Defines the dedicated goal region of a description.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Simulation_Reasoner
object: A Simulation-based Reasoner is a simulation that is used as a reasoner, where the explicit knowledge corresponds to the initial situation, and the implicit knowlegde corresponds to the situation that is derived from that by simulating some unfolding processes.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#coOccurs
object:
A schematic relation between any events that also implies that one event is temporally contained in the other.

Sub-properties are used to distinct between different cases of event endpoint relations that hold for different types of co-occurance.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ForceInteraction
object: Talmy, Leonard (1981) ‘Force Dynamics’. Language and Mental Imagery. May 1981, University of California, Berkeley.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AttentionShift
object: A mental task in which the executing Agent shifts his attention from some Information to another.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DeviceStateRange
object: This class defines the values that a device state can take.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTaskAffordedBy
object: Relates a disposition to the task defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#StateTransition
object: A transition between two states brought about by the Action of some Agent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#before
object: A relation between entities, expressing a 'sequence' schema where one of the entities strictly ends before the other one.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Color
object: The color of an object. Color regions encode the color value in some space such as RGB or HSV, and may further be used to classify the color as red, dark, etc. The color of an object may have different facets, e.g. a red and blue color.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasAnswer
object: The relation between a message and its answer.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTerminalStateOf
object: A relation recording that a Situation was where a Transition ended.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#includesRecord
object: A relationship indicating that an Event has been recorded by an InformationObject

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasRadius
object: The radius of a circular or oval shape.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AgentRole
object:
A role classifying an Agent responsible for performing an Action.

The entity playing an AgentRole is endowed with sentience and the capacity to deliberately choose actions in pursuit of goals. This distinguishes Agents from other causes that could bring an event about.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isParentLinkOf
object: Relates a joint to the link it connects which is closer to the root of the kinematic chain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Placing
object: Distinguished from Positioning in that this task is more about placing an object at a functionally specified location (e.g., place the cup on the table) as opposed to positioning an object at a location defined by coordinates or a region of coordinates (position the cup at xyz).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isSpaceRegionFor
object: Relates a space region to an entity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FileConfiguration
object: A configuration whose members are all files. Used to model, e.g., concrete collections of zip- and jar-files (and so on).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affordsConcept
object: A relation between a disposition and a concept defined in the affordance that describes the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SphereShape
object: A round solid figure with every point on its surface equidistant from its centre.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isDesignedBy
object: A special relation between a Design and an Object, to indicate that the Object is described by the Design.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Size
object: The magnitude or dimension of a thing which can be measured as length, width, height, diameter, perimeter, area, volume.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#relatesToAnotherRole
object: Simple top-level property for relations between two roles.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#meets
object: A relation between entities, expressing a 'sequence' schema where one of the entities exactly ends where the other entity starts.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isStateTypeOf
object: A relation between roles and state types, e.g. 'the chair is the supporter of the person sitting on it'.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ConditionalSuccedence
object:
A relation that holds between two OGPTasks that belong to the same OGPWorkflow, and which means that, if a condition is met, the successor task invocation is to be executed after the predecessor task invocation completes.

The condition is a conjunction of CounterfactualBindings. These bindings may be RoleRoleBindings (meaning, test whether the fillers for these Roles/Parameters are the same) or RoleFillerBindings (meaning, test whether the filler of the Role unifies with the candidate Entity).

An empty conjunction of CounterfactualBindings is assumed to be True.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#HasQualityRegion
object: todo(DB): added for NEEMs (quale change), but not sure yet about it...

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#containsEvent
object: `A contains event B` means that A strictly starts before, and ends after B, i.e. B is wholly contained in A.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isFeatureOf
object: Associates a feature to the physical object it belongs to.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#BeneficiaryRole
object: A role classifying an agent for whose benefit an action is performed.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isMassAttributeOf
object: A relation between physical objects and their mass.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Software
object:
We see Software as the Design of a DesignedTool: the running instance of said Software. Software as a design also follows the Function-Behaviour-Structure model:

The Function is the purpose or problem solving embodied by the Software Instance, e.g., sorting a list.

The Behaviour are the algoirthms used by the Software Instance, e.g., Bubble Sort.

The Structure is the organization of files, classes, objects and method calls of the program code.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isParameterDefinedIn
object: A relation between a description and a parameter.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isEventTypeDefinedIn
object:
A relation between an event type and a description, e.g. an event that is described by the Affordance of an object to be cut with a knife.

The distinction to 'is task defined in' is necessary to let Dispositions and Affordances not only describe which tasks might be afforded by objects, but also whihc processes (where there is no agent). For example, the fall of a knife from a shelf slicing a loaf of bread on impact is , in the absence of an executing agent, not a task but merely a process, the possibility of which is nevertheless described by the dispositions of the knife and the loaf.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#API_Specification
object:
An application programming interface (API) is a way for two or more computer programs to communicate with each other. It is a type of software interface, offering a service to other pieces of software. A document or standard that describes how to build or use an API is called an API specification.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isJointStateOf
object: Relates a joint to its state.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Restrictor
object: A role classifying an object used to deny access to some other entity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isNetForceOf
object: A relation between a physical object and the total force acting on it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Planning
object: A Mental task in which the Agent endeavours to create a sequence of actions for itself which, if followed, will bring about a particular state of affairs in the world. This particular state of affairs is known to the agent and is often called the goal state of the planning action. Planning commits itself to feasibility: the Agent attempts to find a sequence of actions that it believes it will actually be able to perform.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Serving
object: The task in which the agent delivers an object to a physical agent

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isInitialSceneOf
object: A relation between StateTransitions and Scenes, which identifies the scene the transition starts from.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SocialState
object:
A State which describes how Agents relate to each other.

One can argue that any Social state is a Physical state, since anything the Agents may use to construct a social relationship is made of physical things. The difference is that the physical support of the social relationships is not important here, what matters instead is the nature and content of the social relations, regardless of how they are physically realized.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ForgettingIrrelevantInformation
object: A mental task in which the executing agent aims to clean up its present information by deleting an irrelevant information.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Flying
object: A process type classifying a motion of a body that, through its own power, keeps itself aloft.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#IntermediateGrasp
object: A kind of grasp that acquires kinematic control over the gripped object, but without attempting to achieve either strong holding force nor precision of subsequent movement of the gripped object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RestrictedObject
object: An object with restrictions to access something.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasNextStep
object: An ordering relation between tasks in a workflow, saying that a task is followed by another.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl/NonmanifestedSituation
object:
A Situation which does not manifest in any event.

The main use case for this is to represent expectations that are not met, e.g. unfulfilled post-conditions of an action. An action with unmet postconditions is then a failure.

Because of open world semantics of DL, the default assumption for a Situation individual with no "manifests in" relations is simply that we don't know yet whether that Situation is manifested and if so by what Event.

As such, an explicit assertion is needed to make a Situation a nonmanifested one: either declare that individual's type NonmanifestedSituation, or assert that it has 0 manifestsIn relations.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasQuale
object: Relates a quality to its "value", called quale, which is an atomic quality region.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#UndirectedMotion
object: A Motion of a physical Entity for which a destination or path are unknown and/or considered irrelevant; the important aspect about this Motion is simply that it occurs, rather than where it is headed or how it proceeds towards it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#UsageGuideline
object:
Provides a definition, or usage guideline, aimed at a particular community of the ontology's users. The community is identified by the subproperty of UsageGuideline.

A style recommendation for usage guidelines is that they should be brief. In contrast to usual concept annotations that can, and should be detailed about the reasons behind modelling decisions, usage guidelines are simply meant to answer questions about when it is appropriate to use a concept, and they must be a practical, easy to query and understand resource.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#containsObject
object: A spatial relation holding between a container, and objects it contains.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PuttingDown
object: A task in which an Agent puts down an object they have kinematic control over, e.g. a grasped object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Opening
object: A task in which an Agent manipulates a container so as to expose its interior.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ConnectedObject
object: An object that is combined with another object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DesignedContainer
object: An item designed to be able to hold some other items, preventing their free movement and/or protecting them from outside influence. Containers may be used for storage, or to obtain control over items that are otherwise hard to manipulate directly (e.g. liquids).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Enclosing
object: The disposition of an object (the container) to contain other objects by enclosing them to prevent their free movement.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Coverage
object: The disposition of an object (the cover) to hide or to protect objects by covering them. An example is a door that covers items in a container to e.g. prevent dust getting inside of the container.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PushingDown
object: A task in which an Agent pushes an object downwards.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CausalEventRole
object:
A role filled by a description of some action or process that brings about a motion.

As an example, consider the utterance "the tennisman served the ball by hitting it with the racket." In this utterance, the filler of the CausalEventRole is expressed by the "by hitting it with the racket" constituent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Stirring
object: A task in which an agent dissolves small particles like sugar or salt in fluid

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isLinkedTo
object: A spatial relation holding between objects that are linked with each other such that they resist spatial separation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalState
object: A State describing how Entities in the physical world relate to each other.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutionStateRegion
object: A region containing labels that describe different states in the evolution/completion of a task execution.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutionState_Pending
object: The execution state of a pending activity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Connectivity
object: The disposition of an object (the connected object) to establish a connection with others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalAcquiring
object:
The goal of this task is to make some object usable for other tasks, by possibly changing its physical state. Usually, it overlaps some task that describes the manner in which an object is obtained.

The prototypical example of PhysicalAcquiring is picking up an object.

Note that buying an object is NOT PhysicalAcquiring. Buying, or ownership transfer in general, also involves an adjustment in social structures describing ownership.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PickingUp
object: A task in which the Agent uses one or more of its grippers to grasp a usually stationary object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DeviceTurnedOn
object: A value indicating a device is in operation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Transporting
object: A task by which an Agent carries an item from a source to a destination location.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasTerminalSituation
object: A relation between SituationTransitions and Situations, which identifies the Situation the transition ends at.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ImageSchemaTheory
object:
A theory that describes an image-schematic relationship between some entities.

Image schemas are considered as fundamental, pre-conceptual, building blocks of cognition. They were introduced to characterize how human beings are believed to organize and make sense of experience.

For SOMA, whereas the focus of executable schematic theories is to describe how an agent might act, image schematic theories focus on descriptions of how objects behave in the absence of, or after, an active intervention from an agent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasEndLink
object: Relates an object to kinematic components at the end of the kinematic chain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasSoftwareAgent
object: A relation from an Event and the SoftwareAgent responsible for making that Event happen.

http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Accident
