subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Pushing
object: A task in which an Agent moves an object in a direction loosely from the the contact point between agent and object towards object's center of mass. todo: define subclass 'PushingOver'? Would we expect two distinct contacts with the same surface then?

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#NetForce
object: The accumulated force acting upon an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#HumanActivityRecording
object: An episode in which one or more human beings perform an activity and are recorded doing so.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MetacognitiveMonitoring
object: The task to label the processes and states of the own mind, e.g., to interprete the feeling of knowing an information but not being able to retrieve it at the moment as a tip-of-the-tongue event.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Positioning
object: A task in which an Agent places an object at a particular position.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DesignedTool
object: An item designed to enable some action, in which it will play an instrumental role.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RelatumRole
object: Denotes the reference object in a spatial or spatio-temporal schema, i.e. the object with secondary focal prominence. Terminological variants: Ground (Talmy 1983), Landmark (Langacker 1986).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SocialState
object:
Note here a distinction: the Agents involved must be able to communicate. This is because while it is often assumed that an Agent has or aspires to have similar cognitive capacities to a human, This need not be the case; in particular, not all Agents need to maintain theories of mind about each other and therefore not all Agents need to communicate with each other. It is hard to see what sort of meaning Social concepts might have to such Agents, since Social concepts are all about shared constructions.

Note also that the DUL SocialAgent class is not an appropriate restriction however. SocialAgent is one that exists by agreement of PhysicalAgents. For example, a corporation or a nation are SocialAgents. An Agent with the capability to engage socially is not necessarily a DUL SocialAgent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FaultySoftware
object: A description of a situation where some software has a bug.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isOutputParameterFor
object: A relation from a Parameter to an EventType (typically, a Task). The parameter describes an outcome of the event classified by the EventType.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#LocatumRole
object: Denotes the object with primary focal prominence in a spatial or spatio-temporal schema. Terminological variants that appear in the literature on cognitive linguistics include Figure (Talmy 1983) and Trajector (Langacker 1986).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Structured_Text
object: Any Text that adheres to some rules that are in any way more specific than natural language and that cannot be made sense of without knowing said rules.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesParticipant
object:
A Description definesParticipant a Concept to classify participants in Events associated to that Description.

The prototypical example is a Task, which is a concept to classify Actions (a form of Event). A Task may define several Roles, with which to classify participants in the event of that Task's execution.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Configuration
object:
A description of a State. This includes e.g. what acceptable regions for participant objects of the State might look like.
A configuration of the world is construed to be stable on its own. Outside disturbances may cause state transitions, and the settling into some other, self-stable configuration.

Several other Description subclasses may function as Configurations. For example, a Goal is a description of a desired State. A Norm describes a State that should be maintained. A Diagnosis describes a State that causes certain symptoms etc.

Note a couple of issues here. First one relates to what "configuration" means; in particular, this doesn't mean a configuration that is unchanging according to any viewpoint. The analogy here is the "macrostate" from thermodynamics: a macrostate with two gases mixed does not mean all gas particles are motionless, but rather that the locations and movements of gas particles are such that any particle is likely to have as many neighbors of one type as the other.

The second issue relates to what is "outside". The state is a configuration of some, but not necessarily all, Entities in the world. Entities not in this configuration are outside of it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isColorOf
object: Relates a color quality to the object the color belongs to.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ServerRole
object:
The Client-server model is a distributed application structure that partitions tasks or workloads between the providers of a resource or service, called servers, and service requesters, called clients Often clients and servers communicate over a computer network on separate hardware, but both client and server may reside in the same system. A server host runs one or more server programs, which share their resources with clients. A client usually does not share any of its resources, but it requests content or service from a server. Clients, therefore, initiate communication sessions with servers, which await incoming requests. Examples of computer applications that use the client-server model are email, network printing, and the World Wide Web.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Client%E2%80%93server_model

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isEndLinkOf
object: Relates an object to kinematic components at the end of the kinematic chain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InductiveReasoning
object:
A task in which the Agent endeavors to accumulate confidence in some general statement about the world, by gathering instances in which this general statement appears to apply. Note that perfect confidence can never be guaranteed by induction.

Induction is often described as a move from many "specifics" (swan A is white, swan B is white, swan C is white, ...) to the "general" (all swans are white).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloud
object: A task in which an Agent, while in the course of performing some other task(s), reports on their own decision processes that guide this other task(s) for the benefit of an outside observer.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CommunicationReport
object: A task in which an Agent endeavors to describe truthfully some state of affairs.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasBindingFiller
object:
Indicates that an Entity is described by a Binding, in that it is associated with the Role/Parameter that the Binding binds it to. The Binding is only valid in some descriptive context such as a Workflow or Narrative.

Note, the filler can be a Role/Parameter as well, and there are two distinct interpretations, depending on whether the Binding is a RoleRoleBinding or a RoleFillerBinding. See the comments on Binding for more details.

Only RoleFillerBindings can have general Entities as fillers. RoleRoleBindings can only connect to Roles or Parameters via this property.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#GraspTransfer
object: A task in which an Agent switches which of its end effectors holds an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasShape
object: Relates an object to its shape quality.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DepositedObject
object: An object placed ontop of another one.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#GraphQueryLanguage
object: A Query Language that is designed for communication with some Graph Database.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTerminalSceneOf
object: A relation between StateTransitions and Scenes, which identifies the scene the transition is expected to end at.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SupportedObject
object: An object that is supported by some supporter.

subject: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/DUL.owl#hasPostcondition
object: This should be taken to mean that the postcondition is the situation expected to follow the current situation. Whether the expectation is met is another issue.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Avoiding
object: A task in which an Agent moves so as to not enter or pass through a location.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PluginRole
object:
In the Plug-in-Host pattern, a Host application provides services which the Plug-in can use, including a way for Plug-ins to register themselves with the Host application and a protocol for the exchange of data withPplug-ins. Plug-ins depend on the services provided by the host application and do not usually work by themselves. Conversely, the host application operates independently of the plug-ins, making it possible for end-users to add and update plug-ins dynamically without needing to make changes to the host application.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plug-in_(computing)

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MedicalDiagnosis
object: A functional diagnosis of an organism.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#QueryLanguage
object:
Query languages, are Computer languages used to make queries in databases and information systems (Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Query_language).

Note that despite their name, Query languages typically come with syntax and semantic to not only ask for information, but also provide them, e.g., via SQL Update. In that sense, the term "query" from above refers to any formal object of information exchange with a database.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MeshShapeData
object: An InformationObject containing data about the geometry of a physical object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InferenceRules
object: The role of an object that is used to derive a conclusion from some premises.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isRootLinkOf
object: Relates an object to kinematic components at the root of the kinematic chain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Dropping
object:
The dropped object falls mainly under the influence of gravity. However, an agent may also drop something during navigation. The difference to 'Throwing' is that there is no 'Limb motion' which is a constitiuent of the action.

'Dropping' is intentional. Dropping by accident may not has a phase to release the grasp. It could be that the grasp was not strong enough and the objects "slips" away.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#System
object:
A system is a group of interacting or interrelated elements that act according to a set of rules to form a unified whole.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/System

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isInputParameterFor
object: A relation between a Task and one of its input parameters.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Storage
object: The disposition of an object (the container) to store other objects. Storage of an object would facilitate several objectives; such as to store objects in a safe or usual place, to prevent the substances e.g. prevention of milk going bad by storing them in a refrigrator.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTriggerAffordedBy
object: Relates a disposition to the trigger role defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Binding
object:
A Relation between Roles/Parameters and their fillers that holds in a particular descriptive context, such as a Workflow or Narrative.

It covers two conceptually related, but somewhat ontologically distinct situations:

-- a binding between two Roles, or two Parameters, with the meaning that in the particular descriptive context where the Binding holds, a filler for one Role/Parameter is also a filler for the other
-- a binding between a Role/Parameter and an Entity able to fill that Role/Parameter, with the meaning that in the particular descriptive context where the Binding holds, the Entity fills the Role/Parameter.

Note: in the second case, the Entity filling the Role/Parameter may be a Role or Parameter itself. This however does NOT reduce to the first case. Consider these examples:

-- (first situation) The accountant is also the lawyer. In this case, there are two roles, and there is a person filling both of them. This is a factual, role-role binding.
-- (second situation, linking to a generic Entity) The accountant is Bob. In this case, there is a factual, role-filler binding asserting who fills the accountant role.
-- (second situation, linking to a role) The newly opened job is accountant. In this case, there is a factual, role-filler binding asserting that some role is filled by another, without making any assertion about the filler of this second role. It is not known, and not important, whether an accountant exists at this time.

There is a further, orthogonal distinction made between:
-- factual: the Binding is asserted to hold in the descriptive context
-- counterfactual: the Binding is used to express conditions in the descriptive context. A counterfactual Binding is not meant as an assertion that the Binding actually holds.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Leg
object: A limb on which an agent walks or stands.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Throwing
object: A task in which an Agent imparts momentum to an object before releasing it so that it flies for some distance unsupported.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CutObject
object: An object being cut down into pieces.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Cover
object: An object used to cover up others, such as a lid used as a cover for a pot.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PlanarJoint
object: A joint that allows motion in a plane perpendicular to an axis.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalEffector
object: A functional part belonging to an Agent and which allows that Agent to act upon its surroundings.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesParameter
object: A relation between a description and a parameter.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#QueryingTask
object: An Illocutionary act where the Sender of the Message does so to trigger the Receiver to return some information that is specified within the content of the Message.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MovingAway
object: A process type classifying a motion by which some Agent puts distance between itself and another object or location.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasGoal
object: A relation from an Entity to a Goal it pursues. Agents can pursue Goals, and Tasks are also construed as pursuing Goals.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#supports
object: Relates a supportee to one of its supporters.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ActionExecutionPlan
object: idea: steps in workflows assert that they are defined by action execution plans.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Client-Server_Specification
object:
An API Secification that describes the well known Client-Server pattern:

The Client-server model is a distributed application structure that partitions tasks or workloads between the providers of a resource or service, called servers, and service requesters, called clients Often clients and servers communicate over a computer network on separate hardware, but both client and server may reside in the same system. A server host runs one or more server programs, which share their resources with clients. A client usually does not share any of its resources, but it requests content or service from a server. Clients, therefore, initiate communication sessions with servers, which await incoming requests. Examples of computer applications that use the client-server model are email, network printing, and the World Wide Web.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Client%E2%80%93server_model

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Destination
object: A role classifying the location where an event or object is directed towards.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Tool
object: A role to classify an object used to modify or actuate others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Obstacle
object: An object used to restrict access to a protected space or group.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasAction
object: A relation from an Action to a component Action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isInitialStateOf
object: A relation recording that a Situation was where a Transition began.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudPerceptionTopic
object: A topic used when an Agent describes what they currently perceive.

subject: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/DUL.owl#InformationObject
object:
In SOMA-compliant systems, the way to use InformationObjects to specify extra data about an individual entity is to employ the 'is about' and 'expresses' properties (or their inverses 'is reference of' and 'is expressed by') and to supply a persistent identifier for a realization of the InformationObject.

As a prototypical example, consider an individual called Action_XYZ, about which we have some data for which the meaning is described by Description_ABC. The data would be an individual InformationObject_DEF, and the following property assertions would hold:

InformationObject_DEF 'is about' Action_XYZ
InformationObject_DEF expresses Description_ABC


Usually, an individual InformationObject would be connected to (at least) an InformationRealization individual. For example, suppose there is such an InformationRealization individual, InformationRealization_123. Then, this individual will have data properties describing its format and persistent identifier

InformationRealization_123 hasPersistentIdentifier 'doi'
InformationRealization_123 hasDataFormat 'urdf'

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Insertion
object: The disposition of an object (the container) to contain other objects that can be inserted into the container through a portal.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isPerformerAffordedBy
object: Relates a disposition to the performer role defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutionState_Cancelled
object: The execution state of a cancelled activity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PowerGrasp
object: An Agent grasps an object, and focuses on obtaining a strong grasping force upon it, resulting in a grasp able to resist significant outside disturbances. This is useful when using tools with which to later exert force on other things, e.g. when hammering nails.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MetaCognitionMemoryTopic
object: A topic used while an Agent describes its own cognitive processes and actions, and which covers descriptions of what memories are involved in them.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ConditionalSuccedence
object: Note: in RobotWorkflows, Tasks typically may have several possible successors, to be selected based on condition-testing.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isLinkOf
object: Relates an object to its kinematic components.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#LookingFor
object: A task by which an Agent uses its perception apparatus to check for the presence of an object in some specified area.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Capacity
object: The maximum amount an object can contain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AssumingArmPose
object: A task by which an Agent arranges one/some/all of its arms according to some configuration.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Shifting
object: The disposition of an object (the tool) to change the localization of others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Order
object: An 'Order' sorts two or more 'Order item's via the relations 'precedes' and 'follows'.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InformationAcquisition
object:
A mental task in which the executing agent acquires some information that was not immediately available to it before.
A synonym might be "Thinking".

Examples include recalling knowledge or inferring some information from other information.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RemovedObject
object: An object that is removed from another.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isQualeOf
object: Relates a quality to its "value", called quale, which is an atomic quality region.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PathRole
object: A role that classifies the path of a motion.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MentalAction
object:
An Event construed as the Agent participant affecting Entities that are representations of actual or potential Entities or Events in the physical world in which the Agent is embodied. These representations are maintained by the Agent participant in the 'Mental action' event.

One could argue Mental actions are all Physical actions, because anything the Agent may use to maintain such representations will be physical things, However, we make this distinction because for Mental actions it is less important to consider the physical support of the representation and how it changes, and more important to track how the information content of the representation changes.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CrackingTheory
object: A schematic theory of how an agent can inflict damage to the surface of an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasChildLink
object: Relates a joint to the link it connects which is closer to the end of the kinematic chain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Origin
object: A role classifying the location where an event or object originated.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasInitialScene
object: A relation between StateTransitions and Scenes, which identifies the scene the transition starts from.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Unsuccessfulness
object: A description of a situation with a goal that was not or not fully achieved by some system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ForceInteraction
object: Classifies events in which two entities interact with each other with a reference to force. One of the entities, the agonist, has a tendency to either set the other entity (the antagonist) into motion, or to keep it still under the influence of some other force. The tendency only manifests in case the agonist is the "stronger entity".

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Material
object: The matter from which a thing is made.

subject: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/DUL.owl#Action
object: The EASE view: an Action is an Event in which an Agent executes some Task, typically defined by a Workflow, towards the achievement of some Goal.

subject: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/DUL.owl#Agent
object:
Generally, agents are goal-directed entities that are able to monitor their environment to select and perform efficient means-ends actions that are available in a given situation to achieve an intended goal. Agency, therefore, implies the ability to perceive and to change the environment of the agent. Crucially, it also entails intentionality to represent the goal-state in the future, equifinal variability to be able to achieve the intended goal-state with different actions in different contexts, and rationality of actions in relation to their goal to produce the most efficient action available (Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agency_(psychology)).

While we follow this definition, we do so loosely: We do not require the intentionality to be sourced by the agent. E.g., a running computer program (see Software instance) can be seen as an actor and therefore participate in Actions, e.g. some Communication Action, while its intentionality has been bestowed upon it from the agents who started the program or gave an input (e.g., via a mouse click) to achieve some goal.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#OrderedElement
object: A 'Singleton' of an entity that 'is ordered by' some 'Order'. An 'Order item' can only 'precede' or 'follow' another 'Order item', encoding the sortation of the entities contained within the 'Order items'. Different 'Order's need to use different 'Order item's.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Affordance
object: A relation between an object (the bearer) and others (the triggers) that describes the disposition of the bearer to be involved in an action execution that also involves some trigger object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CommandingTask
object: An Illocutionary act where the Sender emits some Message with the intent to cause the Receiver to perform some action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Graspability
object: The disposition of an object (e.g. the handle) to afford grasping the object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MeshShape
object: A solid geometrical figure described in a mesh file.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ArchiveFile
object:
An archive file is a computer file that is composed of one or more files along with metadata.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archive_file

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MonitoringJointState
object: A task in which the Agent keeps track of the physical state of its joints, e.g. their positions, velocities, efforts.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affordanceDefines
object: A relation between an Affordance and a Concept (often an EventType).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Surface
object: The outside part or uppermost layer of something.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasSuccessor
object: Indicates that a Task is the successor in a Succedence Relation: that is, it is the Task to execute last.

subject: N61af892572a446f5be1bd99b7c862905
object: A SituationTransition that manifests in some Event also includes an Action. (NOTE (MP): Typically, the Event manifesting it would be that included Action actually so perhaps we can just require that manifestations of SituationTransitions be Actions?)

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CommunicationTopic
object:
A role that appears in communication tasks, and indicates what the communication is about.

CommunicationTopic can only classify a Social object that participates in an Action that is classified as (the execution of) a CommunicationTask.

Note that classifies here is used in the plays-role sense. This isn't to say that the social object, ie the information exchanged in the communication, is an instance of the topic. Rather, the topic role refers to what the information is about.

For example, if the topic of a communication is flowers, this does not mean the words themselves are flowers, merely that, in some sense, they are about flowers.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ContactState
object: Classifies States in which some objects are in contact.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasRootLink
object: Relates an object to kinematic components at the root of the kinematic chain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExperiencerRole
object: A role used in frame semantics to classify agents performing perception actions, or being the subjects affected by some biological process.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isStepOf
object: A relation stating that a task is a step in a workflow.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CausativeRole
object:
A role classifying objects that are responsible in bringing about an event.

The paradigmatic example is the Agent performing an Action -- the Agent is the effective cause of the Action it performs. However, not all objects causing events are agents.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Software_Configuration
object:
The part-whole relationship of Software and its components. Every Software has (at least 1) such configuration that exactly describes all Resources that make up the software (i.e., that are needed for the Software to function).
We support seperate views:
1. The Software Configuration describes all the necessary files, in which it should also be a File Configuration
2. It describes a Software Suit, e.g., 'Open Office' consists of Writer, Calc, Impress etc. Note that thus. Software can consist of other Software - this pattern may also be useful when describing Software Components, e.g., that some Software relies on a Database Software.
3. It describes not the files, but their content (the program code), which can also be seen as the part-whole relationship if one abstracts away from the files.

subject: Nd674f6e40e3a4a4ba69d7463ca2d185f
object: If something is a terminal situation then it must be a manifested situation (regardless of whether it was expected or not).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Finger
object: A limb used for grasping objects.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ModifyingPhysicalObject
object: Superconcept for tasks that involve affecting some state that an object is in (e.g. where it is located), without creating or destroying the object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Flipping
object: The task in which the agent turns an object over by using a tool or by manipulating

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isSupportedBy
object: Relates a supportee to one of its supporters.

subject: N0c44405acf894f37af948279e01ac999
object: The path of the file on a computer system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isOccurrenceOf
object: A relation between an event and an event type, e.g. 'taking the cup from the table' is an occurence of the motion 'approaching'.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Composing
object: The disposition of an object (the tool) to change the compositional structure of others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ColorRegion
object: Encodes the color of an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Query
object: A role played by some Information Realization that carries meaning, where this meaning is a query of some sort.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Catching
object: A task by which an Agent stops a moving object and gains kinematic control over it, usually by grasping.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isDesignFor
object: A special relation between a Design and an Object, to indicate that the Design describes a way to construct the Object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasMassValue
object: The mass value of a physical object in kilogram.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AssertionTask
object: An Illocutionary Act where the Sender emits some Message with the intent to change what the Receiver believes to be true in some context. Often, assertions are of facts about the real world, but this need not be the case. Assertions can communicate what someone believes, or refer to a world that is entirely fictional. In all these cases however, assertions are intended to update the listener's model (of the real world, or of the speaker's beliefs, or of the fictional world etc.).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasBindingRole
object: Indicates that a Role/Parameter is going to be associated to some filler, or other Role/Parameter, by a Binding. The Binding is only valid in some descriptive context such as a Narrative or Workflow.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isAskedBy
object: A relation from a Query to the Agent who asks it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Clean
object: A cleanliness region with values considered as clean.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PerformerRole
object:
A role classifying an Agent responsible for performing an Action.

The entity playing an PerformerRole is endowed with sentience and the capacity to deliberately choose actions in pursuit of goals. This distinguishes Agents from other causes that could bring an event about.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasFeature
object: Associates a physical object to one of its features.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#BodyMovement
object:
Motion described in terms of how parts of an Agent's body move.

As such, this concept can be applied only to motions involving some PhysicalAgent, or body parts of a PhysicalAgent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Protector
object: A role classifying an object that protects another by preventing other entities from coming in contact with the protected object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Computer_Language
object:
A computer language is a formal language used in communication with a computer.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_language

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Natural_Language_Text
object: A Text in a Natural Language.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasTerminalScene
object: A relation between StateTransitions and Scenes, which identifies the scene the transition is expected to end at.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isReactionTo
object:
Simple relationship between two actions to express that the subject (the reaction) would not have occured if it were not for the object (the cause), e.g., a Communication Action classified as an Answering Task is a reaction to another Communication Task classified as a Query Task and would not have occured without the other. An example without Agents involved would be some domino stone would not have toppled without the first one toppling.

When Agents are involved, the relation might be seen as an abstraction of the execution of some plan that arises from changing the agents goal that is due to perceiving the cause. However, currently it is unclear how to model such a pattern and therefore not included in SOMA.

This relation is seen as transitive.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesPerformer
object: Relates an affordance which is a relation between a bearer and a trigger, to the role of the performer when the affordance is manifested.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#causesTransition
object: A Transition between two Situations is always the result of some Event, and the causesTransition relation should be used to record the causal relation from the Event to the Transition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutableFile
object:
An Executable File, sometimes simply referred to as an executable or binary, causes a computer "to perform indicated tasks according to encoded instructions", as opposed to a data file that must be interpreted (parsed) by a program to be meaningful.

The exact interpretation depends upon the use. "Instructions" is traditionally taken to mean machine code instructions for a physical CPU. In some contexts, a file containing scripting instructions (such as bytecode) may also be considered executable.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#starts
object: `A starts B` means that A starts exactly where B starts, and that A strictly ends before B. As in "I start my day with a coffee".

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Intrinsic
object: A physical quality that is independent of context.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasStateType
object: A relation between roles and state types, e.g. 'the chair is the supporter of the person sitting on it'.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#StatusFailure
object: A status indicating the failure during some workflow execution.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#LocutionaryAction
object:
A Locutionary Act is the performance of an utterance (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locutionary_act).

We additionally require a Locutionary Act to be performed by an Agent, not an Actor - this is what sets it apart from a Communication Action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasRGBValue
object: Associates a ColorRegion to numerical data describing the color. This data uses the Red-Green-Blue color space.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Vaporizing
object: Some material transitions from a liquid to a gaseous phase.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isConceptIncludedIn
object: A relation recording that a Concept participates in a Situation in some way.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Taxis
object: An innate behavioural response such as the knee-jerk reflex or the sucking reflex of human infants.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isPlaceInvolvedIn
object: A relation recording that a PhysicalPlace is involved in some Event; typically, this is where the Event is located.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isPhysicallyContainedIn
object: A spatial relation holding between an object (the container), and objects it contains.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#StatisticalReasoner
object: A Statistical Reasoner is a Reasoner that uses statistical or stochastical data to infer implicit information from explicit information. Examples are Hidden Markov Models and Neural Networks.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AbductiveReasoning
object: A task in which the Agent proceeds from some set of statements about a world, and attempts to obtain an explanation for these statements. This explanation is often an inferred cause, such as a final cause or intention. Further, it is often required that there be some guarantees that the explanation produced by AbductiveReasoning have some desirable property, such as being the simplest or most likely given the set of statements to explain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutableSoftware
object: Executable Software is Software that can directly be executed, in comparison to a Software Library, which might only contain functionality via interfaces, but offers no execution entry point.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointPositionMin
object: The minimum position of a joint given in m (prismatic joints) or rad (hinged joints).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasFrictionAttribute
object: A relation between physical objects and their friction attribute.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#after
object: A relation between entities, expressing a 'sequence' schema where one of the entities strictly ends before the other one.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Actuating
object: todo: think about use of tools. force events are generated between artifacts then. also not only the tool would be the 'salient artifact' here.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FloatingJoint
object: A joint that allows motion for all 6 degrees of freedom.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DeviceTurnedOff
object: A value indicating a device is not in operation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Supporter
object: A role classifying an object used to support others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isBearerDefinedIn
object: Relates an affordance which is a relation between a bearer and a trigger, to the role of the bearer when the affordance is manifested.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Fluid
object: A substance with a consistency such that it can flow or diffuse.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Collision
object: A contact event of objects bumping into each other such that their movement is affected.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#overlappedOn
object: A schematic relation between any entities that also implies ordering, e.g. "she has worked into the night".

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#encodes
object: The relation between two Information Objects that have the same meaning, but are formatted differently. E.g., a text written in UTF-8 encodes a text in a natural writing system (letters) and vice versa.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutionState_Failed
object: The execution state of a failed activity.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Lowering
object: A task in which an Agent reduces the elevation at which they hold an item.

subject: http://www.ontologydesignpatterns.org/ont/dul/DUL.owl#hasPrecondition
object: This should be taken to mean: a precondition is a situation without which the current situation would not be possible.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InformationDismissal
object:
A mental task in which the executing agent dismisses some information.

An example is forgetting some knowledge.

subject: N7928ae83e7aa483097daac06eb4dceec
object: If a transition has a terminal situation then it also has a manifestation.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RedColor
object: A color region with dominant red color.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#TemperatureRegion
object: Encodes the temperature of an object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Source_Code
object: The Source Code itself (the specific set of instruction in a human-readable Programming Language), not the file that it is contained in nor the implemented algorithm!

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ParkingArms
object: A task by which an Agent arranges its arms in such a way so as to minimize opportunities for collision while moving through the environment.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExecutableFormat
object: An Executable Format is a File Format that allows computers to directly execute the content. Examples are MZ (DOS) or COFF.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTaskOfCreatedRole
object: A relation between a Task and one of its output roles. The difference to IsTaskOfOutputRole is that the latter is also applicable, e.g., for Deciding between objects, where the selected object is not created, but still an outcome of that task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FailWFUninterpretableTask
object: A particular kind of failure: a task is not recognized and not associated to anything that could execute it, nor to a workflow that could detail its structure into simpler structure.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Introspecting
object: A mentalk task in which an Agent gathers and processes information about its own mental tasks via, e.g., Meta Reasoning.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#6DPose
object: A point in three dimensional space, given as translation in a reference coordinate system, and an orientation of a coordinate system centered at that point relative to the reference coordinate system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Locomotion
object: The Agent repositions their body in the environment.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#JointState
object: The state of a joint in terms of position, velocity of the joint and effort applied to it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SuccessDiagnosis
object: A diagnosis of the fullfilment of a goal that motivates the behavior of a system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FrictionAttribute
object: The resistance that one surface or object encounters when moving over another.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Focusing
object: The mental task to center the attention to some subject.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Pourable
object: The disposition of a fluid or substance which makes it possible to pour it out of a container and into or onto other objects.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isAnsweredBy
object: A relation from a Query to an Agent who answers it.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isAlterationResultOf
object: Relates an action that alters an object to the region that the alteration reached during the action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PosturalMoving
object:
The Agent changes or takes an overall configuration of its body but is otherwise not significantly affecting other objects nor moving a significant amount from its original location.

Posture changes may take place as part of other actions, for example turning when walking.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RecipientRole
object: A role which classifies an agent who receives an object modified or created by an action.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ProcessFlow
object: A description that structures a Process.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isCreatedOutputOf
object: A relation between a created output role and its Task. The difference to isOutputRoleOf is that the latter is also applicable, e.g., for Deciding between objects, where the selected object is not created, but still an outcome of that task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affordsPerformer
object: Relates a disposition to the performer role defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasSpaceParameter
object: Associates a SpaceRegion to some parameter value describing it. This is a fairly generic property, and to capture the semantics of the information associated to the SpaceRegion, its more specific subproperties should be used.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasPreviousStep
object: An ordering relation between tasks in some workflow, stating that a task is preceded by another.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Prospecting
object: A Mental task in which an Agent endeavours to construct a representation of a future state of affairs of the world it is embodied in.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Cutter
object: A role to classify an object used to cut other objects. Usually should poses sharpness as a quality. Execptions are not considered in this context. Such as a wind, water, or other natural agents cutting(eroding) the rocks.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Cleaning
object: This task in which an agent restores all the objects to their destined locations, wiping a specific object

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasPriority
object: A relation asserting some entity has a particular priority.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Containment
object: The disposition of an object (the container) to contain others.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FactualBinding
http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#StaticFrictionAttribute
object: Friction between two touching objects that do not move relative to each other.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affordsSetpoint
object: Relates a disposition to the setpoint parameter defined by the affordance describing the disposition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#GetTaskParameter
object: A task in which an Agent computes some parameter relevant for another task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Executable_Code
object: Executable Code is Code that when compiled / interpreted, has some clear entrance point and can be executed. Note the difference to an Executable File, which is the file that contains such (compiled) code.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#transitionsBack
object: A property which relates a Transient to an Object it both changes from and changes into. This is useful to model objects which, through participation in a process, transform themselves so that an ontological reclassification is necessary, however this transformation is reversible and at the end of the process the objects revert to their previous kind. An example of this is catalysts in chemistry.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Releasing
object: A task in which an agent relinquishes its kinematic control over an object, typically by releasing it from its grasp.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Database
object:
A Database is a Software that organizes a collection of data stored and and allows for access, usually via some query engine.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalAccessibility
object: Classifies States in which an item is placed in a container or protected by a protector, but the placement of the item and container is such that a, usually agentive, accessor may nevertheless reach the item in order to perform a task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#RelationalDatabase
object:
A Relational Database is a Database based on the relational model of data, which organizes data into one or more tables (or "relations") of columns and rows, with a unique key identifying each row.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Relational_database

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#InformationStorage
object:
A mental task in which the executing agent persists some information for later recall, if necessary.

An example is learning new knowledge.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isPreferenceOf
object: Relates a preference quality to the agent the preference belongs to.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#BehavioralDiagnosis
object: A diagnosis of how a system interacts with its world.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Motion
object: An EventType that classifies motion Processes.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#answers
object: The relation between an answering message and the message it answers.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasPreference
object: Relates an agent to its preference quality.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#contains
object: A schematic relation asserting containment, understood in a very broad sense, by one Entity of another. The relation is defined with domain and range of maximum generality, as it is possible to construe containment to apply between Events, between Objects, between Qualities and so on. Care should be taken when using it that the construal of containment makes sense and is useful. If a clearer relation expresses the connection between two Entities, use that relation instead. For example, rather than saying an Event contains an Object, it is probably better to say the Event has that Object as a participant. More specific versions of this relation exist, e.g. containsEvent, so it is likely that there will be few situations where it should be used itself. However, by acting as a superproperty to several relations, it captures a core similarity between these and enables taxonomy-based similarity metrics.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasHSVValue
object: Associates a ColorRegion to numerical data describing the color. This data uses the Hue-Saturation-Value color space.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#TaskInvocation
object: An elementary workflow consisting in the invocation of one single task. It is used as a descriptive context inside of which factual bindings are valid between the task's arguments and other entities (such as the "local variables" of a larger workflow).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#hasJointVelocityLimit
object: The maximum velocity of a joint given in m/s (prismatic joints) or rad/s (hinged joints).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PhysicalTask
object: A task in which a PhysicalAgent affects some physical object.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PreservativeInteraction
object: A force interaction where the agonist has a tendency to keep another object still. An example is 'holding a door closed' where some object interacts with the door to neutralize forces that could set the door into motion.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Succedence
object:
Note: it is possible for a Succedence relation to exist between a TaskInvocation and itself; in this case, both the hasPredecessor and hasSuccessor roles are filled by the same TaskInvocation individual.

Care must be taken with this however, as a natural interpretation of this situation is an infinite loop.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl/preventedBy
object: A relationship indicating a Situation is prevented by another from manifesting.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ControlTheory
object:
A description of functional-spatial configurations where one object controls another object's position in space, e.g. if a pot moves, then the popcorn contained therein moves, as well. Note that the objects do not need to be in direct contact.

Adopted from GUM-4-space (Bateman et al. 2010).

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ImperativeClause
object: A clause which commands some agent to perform a task or bring about a state of affairs.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#File_format
object:
A File Format is a standard way that information is encoded for storage in a computer file. It specifies how bits are used to encode information in a digital storage medium.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_format

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Accident
object:
An Event for which causes are unknown and/or considered irrelevant. This is true also for "final causes" (that is, intentions) of Agents participating in the Accident: it is not the intentions of these Agents to bring about the Accident.

Note a distinction between this definition and some informal, everyday uses of "accident" which require a causal structure and responsibility to be ascertained. An accident, in the informal sense, may require an explanation as to who made a mistake in bringing about the event; a "traffic accident", where we want to know who's responsible, is an example of this.

Such an event does NOT fall under the definition of Accident here. An example of Accident would be a fair coin landing Heads: the causal chain for why this exact face landed is not important, all that matters is the brute fact that the coin landed Heads.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#simultaneous
object: `A simultaneous B` means that A strictly starts and ends at the same time instant as B, i.e. their temporal extend is equal.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Remembering
object:
A Mental task in which the Agent recalls a record of a previous state of affairs in the world.

The Agent must have witnessed and memorized this state of affairs in order to record it. Remembering commits itself to accuracy: the Agent attempts to reconstruct as accurate a record as it can. Note, this does not mean the Agent will communicate the recollection accurately.

The difference to Memory retrieval is that for this Task, we are concerned with knowledge about a previous world state. Memory Retrieval is more general in the sense that it also includes the retrieval of learned facts and rules.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Feature
object: Features are 'parasitic' entities that only exist insofar their host exists. Typical examples are holes, bumps, boundaries, or spots of color.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isPerformerDefinedIn
object: Relates an affordance which is a relation between a bearer and a trigger, to the role of the performer when the affordance is manifested.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#affects
object: Simple relationship between two actions to express that a variation in the course or outcome of the subject (the affector) would have resulted in a variation in the object (the affectee), e.g., a planning task that sets parameters such as goal position affects the subsequently executed pick-and-place task that uses that parameter.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#AnsweringTask
object: An Illocutionary act where the Sender emits some Message to the Receiver as a reaction to some previous Communication task where the Roles where switched, i.e., the Sender (Receiver) of the Answering task has been the Sender (Sender) for the cause.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Predilection
object:
The relation between a 'Preference' and the 'Order' that the 'Preference' defines over Situations.

For the complete model, see 'Preference'.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Status
object: A role that can be played by some parameter which indicates the state of affairs of some entity, e.g. a flag describing the outcome of an action in terms of success or failure, or an indicator of whether a device is turned on or off.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CausedMotionTheory
object:
A schematic theory describing a situation in which an agent performs an action which causes an object to move along a certain path. A popular example being "He sneezed the napkin off the table." (Goldberg 1995)

Let xA, xP be objects filling the agent, patient roles of this schema. Then one can infer that xA movesObject xP.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PrismaticJoint
object: A sliding joint that slides along an axis, and has a limited range specified by the upper and lower limits.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Threshold
object: A role played by a parameter which indicates some value that, when crossed, triggers some condition.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ContinuousJoint
object: A continuous hinge joint that rotates around an axis and has no upper and lower limits.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#interactsWith
object: A relation between objects that interact with each other.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SoftwareInstance
object:
A Software instance is an entity to represent the agent that emerges from and while executing software: Some object, that can perform actions and communicate via some interfaces.
In this view, we see the of an Agent required intentionality its intentionality as bestowed upon the Software instance from the agents who started the program or gave an input (e.g., via a mouse click) to achieve some goal.

Another apporach might be to not model this entity at all and only see Execution of Software as a Process (see, e.g., https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Execution_(computing)). However, this would complicate modeling communication between running Software processes.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#GreenColor
object: A color region with dominant green color.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Computer_Program
object: The Program itself (the specific set of instruction in a Programming Language), not the file that it is contained in nor the implemented algorithm!

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Appliance
object: A device designed to perform a specific task, and that can be operated in some way.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#IllocutionaryTask
object:
A task which is executed by a Locution action: A Locution is what was said and meant, Illocution is what was done.

When somebody says "Is there any salt?" at the dinner table, the illocutionary act is a request: "please give me some salt" even though the locutionary act (the literal sentence) was to ask a question about the presence of salt.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illocutionary_act

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CircularCylinder
object: A cylinder figure with circular cross section.

subject: N6c5af1d52a334acf857819edecd7aca4
object: If a SituationTransition manifests in some Event, then it also has an initial Situation and a terminal one.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Location
object: A role classifying a location of interest, often specified as a spatial relation between several objects, themselves usually classified by spatial relation roles.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#definesEventType
object:
A relation between a description and an event type, e.g. an Affordance of an object to be cut with a knife describes that event.

The distinction to defines task is necessary to let Dispositions and Affordances not only describe which tasks might be afforded by objects, but also whihc processes (where there is no agent). For example, the fall of a knife from a shelf slicing a loaf of bread on impact is , in the absence of an executing agent, not a task but merely a process, the possibility of which is nevertheless described by the dispositions of the knife and the loaf.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Mixing
object: A task by which an Agent combines several entities, such that the combination is difficult or in practice impossible to reverse.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Message
object:
A message is a discrete unit of communication intended by the source for consumption by some recipient or group of recipients (Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Message).

Note that the Role Message classifies the Information Realization, not the content.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#FunctionalControl
object:
Classifies States in which an object restricts the movement of another, at least partially. Usually neither object is construed to be an agent.

Note that this State focuses on how the interaction of, usually non-agentive, objects restricts their motion. This is in contrast to Blockage/Accessibility states where the placement of some objects influences the access to some of them by a third, usually agentive party.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#firstMember
object: A relation between a collection and a member of it that is least according to some ordering. This ordering can be arbitrary, i.e. the order in which Entities are recorded in the Collection.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SupportTheory
object:
An image schematic theory that describes the reified functional relation holding between two spatial objects x and y, such that x physically supports y in the presence of gravity; x and y need not be in contact. An example of such an expression is "The bowl is on the table".

This is also known as FunctionalControlExternal in GUM (Bateman et al. 2010).

Let xL, xR be objects filling the locatum, relatum roles of this schema. Then one can infer that xL isSupportedBy xR.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#DesignedFurniture
object: An object used to make a room or building suitable for living or working.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isInputRoleOf
object: A relation between an input roles and its Task.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CognitiveAgent
object: An agent that is capable to act on its own, in contrast to sub-cognitive Agents, that need to have their intentionality bestowed upon some other agent.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Proprioceiving
object: A task in which the Agent gathers and interprets sensor information about itself.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ThinkAloudGeneralKnowledgeTopic
object: A topic used when an Agent states general knowledge they have.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CylinderShape
object: A solid geometrical figure with straight parallel sides and a circular or oval cross section.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isChildLinkOf
object: Relates a joint to the link it connects which is closer to the end of the kinematic chain.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#EventAdjacentRole
object:
A role classifying a participant in an event.

In linguistics, this is also known as a thematic role.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SoftwareRole
object: A Software Role is a Role applying to only Software and encoding the purpose of the Software: Its Role within Interface Patterns (e.g. Client vs. Server), its functionality (e.g. Database vs. Comnputer Game), and so on.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ArchiveFormat
object:
An Archive Format is the file format of an archive file.

Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archive_file#Archive_formats

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isSituationIncludedIn
object: A relation recording that a Situation participates in another in some role, or can be considered as a subsituation of the other.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#ExtractedObject
object: An object that is removed from a container or system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#isTriggerDefinedIn
object: Relates an affordance which is a relation between a bearer and a trigger, to the role of the trigger when the affordance is manifested.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Markup_Language
object:
Markup refers to data included in an electronic document which is distinct from the document's content in that it is typically not included in representations of the document for end users, for example on paper or a computer screen, or in an audio stream. Markup is often used to control the display of the document or to enrich its content to facilitate automated processing. A markup language is a set of rules governing what markup information may be included in a document and how it is combined with the content of the document in a way to facilitate use by humans and computer programs.

From Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markup_language

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#TechnicalDiagnosis
object: A functional diagnosis of a technical system.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#CounterfactualBinding
object:
CounterfactualBindings are used to express conditions:

-- that two roles share a filler (RoleRoleBindings);
-- that the filler of a role is a particular entity (RoleFillerBindings). This is typically the case when the filler of the role may be one of a few constants, as is the case with the execution status of a robot task.

TODO: for the robot workflows we are likely to need at the start, testing equality of fillers is enough. In the future, we may want to replace that with unifiability of fillers.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#PreferenceRegion
object: The 'Region' of 'Preference's, containing all possible 'Order's between all possible 'Situation's.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#MetaCognitionPlanningTopic
object: A topic used while an Agent describes the planning it does for its own cognitive processes and actions.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#SelfReflection
object: The task of evaluating the personal cognitive processes.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Arm
object: A limb used to reach for objects.

subject: http://www.ease-crc.org/ont/SOMA.owl#Retracting
object: A task in which an Agent moves its arms away from a location.
